bookInfo.name: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: 資治通鑑 第255卷

translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 255
translations.idiomatic: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 255

sentences.zh: 【唐紀七十一】　起玄黓攝提格五月，盡閼逢執徐五月，凡二年有奇。

translations.literal: [Tang Records 71] Beginning in the fifth month of the year Xuan'yuan She'tige, ending in the fifth month of the year E'feng Zhixu, altogether a little more than two years.
translations.idiomatic: [Tang Records 71] From the fifth month of the third year of Guangming (883) through the fifth month of the first year of Zhonghe (884)—a span of slightly more than two years.

sentences.zh: 五月，以湖南觀察使閔勖權充鎭南節度使。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Min Xu, the Hunan observation commissioner, was appointed acting military governor of Zhennan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, Min Xu, commissioner of Hunan, was named acting military governor of Zhennan.

sentences.zh: 勖屢求於湖南建節，朝廷恐諸道觀察使效之，不許。

translations.literal: Xu had repeatedly requested that a military commission be established in Hunan; the court feared that observation commissioners in other circuits would follow his example and did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: Xu had long pressed for a full military governorship in Hunan, but the court refused, fearing other regional commissioners would demand the same.

sentences.zh: 先是，王仙芝寇掠江西，高安人鍾傳聚蠻獠，依山爲堡，眾至萬人。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Wang Xianzhi raided Jiangxi, Zhong Chuan of Gao'an gathered Man and Liao tribesmen, built mountain fortresses, and his following reached ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, during Wang Xianzhi's raids in Jiangxi, Zhong Chuan of Gao'an had rallied tribal fighters, built strongholds in the hills, and gathered a force of ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 仙芝陷撫州而不能守，傳入據之，詔即以爲刺史。

translations.literal: Xianzhi captured Fuzhou but could not hold it; Chuan entered and seized it, and an edict immediately appointed him prefect.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianzhi took Fuzhou but could not keep it, Chuan moved in and held the city; the court at once named him prefect.

sentences.zh: 至是，又逐江西觀察使高茂卿，據洪州。

translations.literal: At this time he again drove out Jiangxi observation commissioner Gao Maoqing and seized Hongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: By then he had also expelled Gao Maoqing, the Jiangxi observation commissioner, and seized Hongzhou.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以勖本江西牙將，故復置鎭南軍，使勖領之。

translations.literal: Because Xu had originally been a Jiangxi military adjutant, the court re-established the Zhennan army and had Xu lead it.
translations.idiomatic: Since Xu was himself a former Jiangxi staff officer, the court revived the Zhennan command and put him in charge of it.

sentences.zh: 若傳不受代，令勖因而討之。

translations.literal: If Chuan would not accept replacement, they ordered Xu to take the opportunity to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: If Chuan refused to step down, Xu was to use the appointment as a pretext to attack him.

sentences.zh: 勖知朝廷意欲斗二盜使相斃，辭不行。

translations.literal: Xu knew the court intended to set the two bandits fighting so they would destroy each other, and declined to go.
translations.idiomatic: Xu saw that the court meant to pit the two rebels against each other and declined the assignment.

sentences.zh: 加淮南節度使高駢兼侍中，罷其鹽鐵轉運使。

translations.literal: Gao Pian, military governor of Huainan, was additionally appointed grand counselor and removed from his post as salt and iron transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Pian of Huainan was made grand counselor as well, but stripped of his lucrative salt monopoly.

sentences.zh: 駢既失兵柄，又解利權，攘袂大詬，遣其幕僚顧雲草表自訴，言辭不遜，其略曰：「是陛下不用微臣，固非微臣有負陛下。」

translations.literal: Pian, having lost military authority and also been stripped of profitable power, rolled up his sleeves and cursed loudly; he sent his staff member Gu Yun to draft a memorial of self-defense with insubordinate language, the gist of which said: "It is that Your Majesty does not use this humble servant—it is certainly not that this humble servant has failed Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: Deprived of both command and the salt revenues, Pian flew into a rage and had his aide Gu Yun draft a defiant memorial. It began: "Your Majesty chose not to use me; I have not failed Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「奸臣未悟，陛下猶迷，不思宗廟之焚燒，不痛園陵之開毀。」

translations.literal: It also said: "Treacherous ministers have not awakened, and Your Majesty is still deluded, not reflecting on the burning of the ancestral temples and not grieving over the opening and destruction of the imperial tombs."
translations.idiomatic: He went on: "Villains still hold sway, and Your Majesty remains blind—unmoved by the burning of the ancestral shrines, unmoved by the desecration of the imperial tombs."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「王鐸僨軍之將，崔安潛在蜀貪黷，豈二儒士能戢強兵！」

translations.literal: It also said: "Wang Duo is a general of a defeated army; Cui Anqian in Shu is greedy and corrupt—how can two Confucian scholars restrain powerful troops!"
translations.idiomatic: He wrote: "Wang Duo commands a beaten army; Cui Anqian in Shu is corrupt—what can two bookish officials do against hardened troops?"

sentences.zh: 又曰：「今之所用，上至帥臣，下及裨將，以臣所料，悉可坐擒。」

translations.literal: It also said: "Those now employed, from supreme commanders down to subordinate generals—in my estimation, all could be captured without rising from one's seat."
translations.idiomatic: He added: "Every commander you have appointed now, from the top down, could be taken without a fight—or so I judge."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「無使百代有抱恨之臣，千古留刮席之恥。

translations.literal: It also said: "Do not let a hundred generations have a minister who harbors resentment, or leave for a thousand years the shame of having one's mat scraped aside.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded: "Do not leave posterity a minister nursing a grievance, or history the shame of a loyal man turned away at the door.

sentences.zh: 臣但慮寇生東土，劉氏復興，即軹道之災，豈獨往日！」

translations.literal: This humble servant only fears that bandits will arise in the eastern lands and the Liu house will revive—that the disaster of Zhidao is not confined to days past alone!"
translations.idiomatic: I fear only that rebels will rise in the east and the Han will rise again—the calamity of Zhidao is not a thing of the distant past alone!"

sentences.zh: 又曰：「今賢才在野，憸人滿朝，致陛下爲亡國之君，此子等計將安出！」

translations.literal: It also said: "Now the worthy are in the wilds while slanderers fill the court, making Your Majesty a ruler of a perishing state—what schemes are these people plotting!"
translations.idiomatic: He concluded: "Talent languishes in obscurity while flatterers pack the court—you are being made the last emperor of a dying dynasty. What are these men plotting?"

sentences.zh: 上命鄭畋草詔切責之，其略曰：「綰利則牢盆在手，主兵則都統當權，直至京北、京西神策諸鎭，悉在指揮之下，可知董制之權。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Zheng Tian to draft an edict sternly rebuking him, the gist of which said: "When you controlled profits the salt monopoly was in your hands; when you commanded troops you held supreme command—all the way to the Shence garrisons north and west of the capital, all were under your direction. One can see how great your power was.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had Zheng Tian draft a sharp rebuke. It read in part: "You held the salt revenues in your grasp and supreme command over the armies—even the Shence garrisons about the capital answered to you. Your power was absolute.

sentences.zh: 而又貴作司徒，榮爲太尉。

translations.literal: Moreover you were ennobled as minister of education and honored as grand marshal.
translations.idiomatic: You were made Minister of Education and Grand Marshal besides.

sentences.zh: 以爲不用，如何爲用乎？」

translations.literal: If this is called not being used, then what would count as being used?"
translations.idiomatic: If that is not being used, what would you call it?"

sentences.zh: 又曰：「朕緣久付卿兵柄，不能翦蕩元兇，自天長漏網過淮，不出一兵襲逐，奄殘京國，首尾三年。

translations.literal: It also said: "We long entrusted you with military authority, yet you could not exterminate the chief villain. Since Huang Chao slipped through at Tianchang and crossed the Huai, you sent not a single soldier in pursuit; he ravaged the capital region for three years in all.
translations.idiomatic: The edict went on: "I entrusted you with command for years, yet you failed to destroy the rebel leader. After Huang Chao escaped at Tianchang and crossed the Huai, you never sent a man in pursuit while he laid waste to the capital—for three full years.

sentences.zh: 廣陵之師，未離封部，忠臣積望，勇士興譏，所以擢用元臣，誅夷臣寇。」

translations.literal: Your Guangling troops never left your jurisdiction; loyal ministers accumulated resentment and brave warriors raised ridicule. Therefore we promoted great ministers and punished rebellious subjects."
translations.idiomatic: Your army at Yangzhou never left your own territory. Loyal officials grew bitter; soldiers mocked you. That is why we promoted others and stripped you of power."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「從來倚仗之意，一旦控告無門，凝睇東南，惟增淒惻！」

translations.literal: It also said: "Our long-standing reliance on you—suddenly you have no avenue of appeal; gazing fixedly toward the southeast, we only feel added sorrow!"
translations.idiomatic: It added: "We had leaned on you for so long—now you rail at us with nowhere left to turn. We look toward the southeast and can only grieve."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「謝玄破苻堅於淝水，裴度平元濟於淮西，未必儒臣不如武將。」

translations.literal: It also said: "Xie Xuan defeated Fu Jian at the Fei River; Pei Du pacified Wu Yuanji in Huaixi—Confucian ministers are not necessarily inferior to military generals."
translations.idiomatic: The edict reminded him: "Xie Xuan routed Fu Jian at the Fei River; Pei Du crushed Wu Yuanji in Huaixi—civil officials are not always weaker than generals."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「宗廟焚燒，園陵開毀，龜玉毀櫝，誰之過歟！」

translations.literal: It also said: "The ancestral temples burned, the imperial tombs opened and destroyed, the tortoise and jade broken in their cases—whose fault is this!"
translations.idiomatic: It demanded: "The shrines burned, the tombs violated, the regalia shattered—whose fault is that?"

sentences.zh: 又曰：「『奸臣未悟』之言，何人肯認！

translations.literal: It also said: "As for the words 'treacherous ministers have not awakened'—who would acknowledge them!
translations.idiomatic: On his charge that "villains still hold sway," the edict asked: "Who would admit to that?

sentences.zh: 『陛下猶迷』之語，朕不敢當！」

translations.literal: As for the words 'Your Majesty is still deluded'—We dare not accept them!"
translations.idiomatic: As for saying Your Majesty is still deluded—I will not hear it!"

sentences.zh: 又曰：「卿尚不能縛黃巢於天長，安能坐擒諸將！」

translations.literal: It also said: "You could not even bind Huang Chao at Tianchang—how can you capture all the generals without rising!"
translations.idiomatic: It taunted him: "You could not even seize Huang Chao at Tianchang—how can you claim every general could be taken without a fight?"

sentences.zh: 又曰：「卿雲劉氏復興，不知誰爲魁首？

translations.literal: It also said: "You say the Liu house will revive—do you not know who would be its leader?
translations.idiomatic: On his warning of a Han restoration: "Who do you imagine would lead it?

sentences.zh: 比朕於劉玄、子嬰，何太誣罔！」

translations.literal: To compare Us to Liu Xuan and Ziying—how excessively slanderous!"
translations.idiomatic: To compare me to Liu Xuan and Emperor Ziying—is slander beyond measure!"

sentences.zh: 又曰：「況天歩未傾，皇綱尚整，三靈不昧，百度俱存，君臣之禮儀，上下之名分，所宜遵守，未可墮陵。

translations.literal: It also said: "Moreover Heaven's step has not yet toppled, the imperial net is still intact, the three spirits are not obscured, and the hundred offices all remain. The ritual between ruler and minister and the names of superior and inferior ought to be observed—you must not fall into insolence.
translations.idiomatic: The edict concluded: "The dynasty still stands, the realm's order endures, the spirits are not abandoned, and government goes on. Ruler and subject still have their roles—you must not forget yours.

sentences.zh: 朕雖沖人，安得輕侮！」

translations.literal: Though We are a young ruler, how can We be lightly insulted!"
translations.idiomatic: Young though I am, I will not be insulted with impunity!"

sentences.zh: 駢臣節既虧，自是貢賦遂絶。

translations.literal: Pian's loyalty as a subject having been compromised, from then on tribute and taxes ceased.
translations.idiomatic: With his loyalty forfeit, Pian stopped sending tribute to the court altogether.

sentences.zh: 以天平留後曹存實爲節度使。

translations.literal: Cao Cunshi, acting military governor of Tianping, was appointed military governor.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cunshi, acting governor of Tianping, was confirmed as military governor.

sentences.zh: 黃巢攻興平，興平諸軍退屯奉天。

translations.literal: Huang Chao attacked Xingping; the various armies at Xingping withdrew and encamped at Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Chao attacked Xingping, and the government forces there fell back to Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 加河陽節度使諸葛爽同平章事。

translations.literal: Zhuge Shuang, military governor of Heyang, was additionally appointed associate chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Shuang of Heyang was made associate chief minister as well.

sentences.zh: 六月，以涇原留後張鈞爲節度使。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Zhang Jun, acting military governor of Jingyuan, was appointed military governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, Zhang Jun, acting governor of Jingyuan, was confirmed as military governor.

sentences.zh: 荊南節度使段彥謨與監軍朱敬玫相惡，敬玫別選壯士三千人，號忠勇軍，自將之。

translations.literal: Duan Yanmo, military governor of Jingnan, and the army supervisor Zhu Jingmei were on bad terms; Jingmei separately selected three thousand stalwart men, called them the Loyal and Brave Army, and led them himself.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Yanmo, governor of Jingnan, feuded with the army supervisor Zhu Jingmei, who raised three thousand picked troops as the Loyal and Brave Army and commanded them personally.

sentences.zh: 彥謨謀殺敬玫；

translations.literal: Yanmo plotted to kill Jingmei;
translations.idiomatic: Yanmo plotted to kill Jingmei;

sentences.zh: 己亥，敬玫先帥眾攻彥謨，殺之，以少尹李燧爲留後。

translations.literal: on the day jihai, Jingmei first led his troops to attack Yanmo, killed him, and appointed Vice Prefect Li Sui acting military governor.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai, Jingmei struck first, killed Yanmo, and installed Vice Prefect Li Sui as acting governor.

sentences.zh: 蜀人羅渾擎、句胡僧、羅夫子各聚眾數千人以應阡能，楊行遷等與之戰，數不利，求益兵。

translations.literal: The Shu men Luo Hunqing, Gou Huseng, and Luo Fuzi each gathered followings of several thousand to join Qian Neng; Yang Xingqian and others fought them, met repeated defeats, and requested more troops.
translations.idiomatic: In Shu, Luo Hunqing, Gou Huseng, and Luo Fuzi each raised thousands to support Qian Neng. Yang Xingqian's forces fought them repeatedly without success and asked for reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 府中兵盡，陳敬瑄悉搜倉庫門庭之卒以給之。

translations.literal: The prefectural troops were exhausted; Chen Jingxuan searched out every man from the warehouses and gatehouses to supply them.
translations.idiomatic: With the garrison spent, Chen Jingxuan scraped together every clerk and gate guard he could find and sent them out.

sentences.zh: 是月，大戰於乾溪，官軍大敗。

translations.literal: That month a great battle was fought at Qianxi; the government army was heavily defeated.
translations.idiomatic: That month the government forces were routed in a major battle at Qianxi.

sentences.zh: 行遷等恐無功獲罪，多執村民爲俘送府，日數十百人。

translations.literal: Fearing punishment for achieving nothing, Xingqian and the others seized many village people as captives and sent them to the prefecture—dozens or hundreds each day.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing punishment for their failures, Xingqian's men seized villagers as captives and sent them to the capital by the dozens or hundreds each day.

sentences.zh: 敬瑄不問，悉斬之。

translations.literal: Jingxuan made no inquiry and had them all beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxuan asked no questions and had them all executed.

sentences.zh: 其中亦有老弱及婦女，觀者或問之，皆曰：「我方治田績麻，官軍忽入村，系虜以來，竟不知何罪！」

translations.literal: Among them were also the old, the weak, and women; when onlookers sometimes asked them, all said: "We were just tending fields and retting hemp when government troops suddenly entered the village, bound us as captives, and brought us here—we do not know what crime we committed!"
translations.idiomatic: The condemned included the elderly, the weak, and women. When spectators asked, they all said: "We were farming and tending hemp when soldiers burst into our village, dragged us away, and we still do not know what crime we committed!"

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，己巳，以鍾傳爲江西觀察使，從高駢之請也。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on the day jisi, Zhong Chuan was appointed Jiangxi observation commissioner, acceding to Gao Pian's request.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, on jisi, Zhong Chuan was made Jiangxi observation commissioner at Gao Pian's urging.

sentences.zh: 傳既去撫州，南城人危全諷復據之，又遣其弟仔倡據信州。

translations.literal: After Chuan left Fuzhou, Wei Quanfeng of Nancheng seized it again, and also sent his younger brother Zichang to seize Xinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Once Chuan left Fuzhou, Wei Quanfeng of Nancheng took it back and sent his brother Zichang to seize Xinzhou as well.

sentences.zh: 尚讓攻宜君寨，會大雪盈尺，賊凍死者什二三。

translations.literal: Shang Rang attacked the Yijun stockade; heavy snow piled a foot deep, and two or three tenths of the rebels froze to death.
translations.idiomatic: Shang Rang attacked Yijun stockade, but a foot of snow fell and killed twenty or thirty percent of his men from exposure.

sentences.zh: 蜀人韓求聚眾數千人應阡能。

translations.literal: The Shu man Han Qiu gathered a following of several thousand to join Qian Neng.
translations.idiomatic: In Shu, Han Qiu raised several thousand men to support Qian Neng.

sentences.zh: 鎭海節度使周寶奏高駢承製以賊帥孫端爲宣歙觀察使。

translations.literal: Zhou Bao, military governor of Zhenhai, reported that Gao Pian had on his own authority appointed the bandit leader Sun Duan as Xuanshe observation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Bao of Zhenhai reported that Gao Pian had unilaterally named the rebel Sun Duan Xuanshe observation commissioner.

sentences.zh: 詔寶與宣歙觀察使裴虔餘發兵拒之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Bao and Xuanshe observation commissioner Pei Qianyu to raise troops to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Bao and Pei Qianyu of Xuanshe to raise troops against Sun Duan.

sentences.zh: 南詔上書請早降公主，詔報以方議禮議。

translations.literal: Nanzhao sent a memorial requesting that the princess be sent down early; the edict in reply said ritual matters were still under discussion.
translations.idiomatic: Nanzhao asked that the princess be sent promptly; the court replied that wedding protocol was still being negotiated.

sentences.zh: 以保大留後東方逵爲節度使，充京城東面行營招討使。

translations.literal: Dongfang Kui, acting military governor of Baoda, was appointed military governor and made eastern capital campaign commander for the eastern circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Dongfang Kui, acting governor of Baoda, was confirmed as military governor and named eastern campaign commander for the capital region.

sentences.zh: 閏月，加魏博節度使韓簡兼侍中。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, Han Jian, military governor of Weibo, was additionally appointed grand counselor.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, Han Jian of Weibo was also made grand counselor.

sentences.zh: 八月，以兵部侍郎、判度支鄭紹業同平章使，兼荊南節度使。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Zheng Shaoye, vice minister of war and acting director of fiscal affairs, was appointed associate chief minister and concurrently military governor of Jingnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, Zheng Shaoye, vice minister of war and fiscal director, was made associate chief minister and military governor of Jingnan as well.

sentences.zh: 漸東觀察使劉漢宏遣弟漢宥及馬歩軍都虞候辛約，將兵二萬營於西陵，謀兼併浙西，杭州刺史董昌遣都知兵馬使錢鏐拒之。

translations.literal: Zhedong observation commissioner Liu Hanhong sent his younger brother Hanyou and cavalry commander Xin Yue with twenty thousand troops to encamp at Xiling, plotting to annex Zhexi; Hangzhou prefect Dong Chang sent his commander of military affairs Qian Liu to resist.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hanhong of eastern Zhejiang sent his brother Hanyou and cavalry commander Xin Yue with twenty thousand men to camp at Xiling, aiming to seize western Zhejiang. Hangzhou's Dong Chang sent Qian Liu to oppose them.

sentences.zh: 壬子，鏐乘霧夜濟江，襲其營，大破之，所殺殆盡，漢宥、辛約皆走。

translations.literal: On the day renzi, Liu crossed the river at night in fog, raided their camp, and routed them; nearly all were killed, and both Hanyou and Xin Yue fled.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi, Liu crossed the river under cover of fog, stormed their camp, and nearly annihilated them. Hanyou and Xin Yue both escaped.

sentences.zh: 魏博節度使韓簡亦有兼併之志，自將兵三萬攻河陽，敗諸葛爽於脩武；

translations.literal: Han Jian, military governor of Weibo, also harbored ambitions of annexation; he personally led thirty thousand troops to attack Heyang and defeated Zhuge Shuang at Xiuwu;
translations.idiomatic: Han Jian of Weibo likewise sought to expand his domain. He led thirty thousand men against Heyang and defeated Zhuge Shuang at Xiuwu.

sentences.zh: 爽棄城走，簡留兵戍之，因掠邢、洺而還。

translations.literal: Shuang abandoned the city and fled; Jian left troops to garrison it, then plundered Xing and Ming and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang abandoned the city and fled. Jian garrisoned it, raided Xing and Ming prefectures, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 李國昌自達靼帥其族遷於代州。

translations.literal: Li Guochang led his clan from the Tatars of Dada to migrate to Daizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guochang led his clan from Dada to settle in Daizhou.

sentences.zh: 黃巢所署同州防禦使朱溫屢請益兵以扞河中，知右軍事孟楷抑之，不報。

translations.literal: Zhu Wen, whom Huang Chao had appointed defense commissioner of Tongzhou, repeatedly requested more troops to defend against Hezhong; Meng Kai, who managed right-wing affairs, suppressed the requests and gave no reply.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Wen, Huang Chao's defense commissioner at Tongzhou, repeatedly asked for reinforcements to hold Hezhong, but Meng Kai, who controlled the right wing, blocked every request.

sentences.zh: 溫見巢兵勢日蹙，知其將亡，親將胡真、謝瞳勸溫歸國。

translations.literal: Wen saw that Chao's military strength daily grew tighter and knew he would perish; his close generals Hu Zhen and Xie Tong urged Wen to return to the Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Huang Chao's cause collapse, Wen knew the rebellion was doomed. His officers Hu Zhen and Xie Tong urged him to defect to the Tang.

sentences.zh: 九月，丙戌，溫殺其監軍嚴實，舉州降王重榮。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the day bingxu, Wen killed his army supervisor Yan Shi and surrendered the whole prefecture to Wang Chongrong.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on bingxu, Wen killed his supervisor Yan Shi and surrendered Tongzhou to Wang Chongrong.

sentences.zh: 溫以舅事重榮，王鐸承製以溫爲同華節度使，使瞳奉表詣行在。

translations.literal: Wen treated Chongrong as a maternal uncle; Wang Duo on imperial authority appointed Wen military governor of Tonghua and sent Tong to present a memorial at the temporary court.
translations.idiomatic: Wen treated Chongrong as a kinsman by marriage. Wang Duo appointed him military governor of Tonghua and sent Xie Tong to the emperor's camp with a submission.

sentences.zh: 瞳，福州人也。

translations.literal: Tong was a man of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Tong was from Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 李詳以重榮待溫厚，亦欲歸之，爲監軍所告。

translations.literal: Li Xiang, because Chongrong treated Wen generously, also wished to surrender to him, but was denounced by the army supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiang, seeing how well Chongrong treated Wen, also wanted to defect, but the army supervisor reported him.

sentences.zh: 黃巢殺之，以其弟思鄴爲華州刺史。

translations.literal: Huang Chao killed him and appointed his younger brother Sixie prefect of Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Chao executed Li Xiang and appointed his brother Sixie prefect of Hua.

sentences.zh: 桂州軍亂，逐節度使張從訓，以前容管經略使崔焯爲嶺南西道節度使。

translations.literal: The Guizhou army mutinied and expelled military governor Zhang Congxun; Cui Zhuo, former Jingguan frontier commissioner, was appointed military governor of Lingnan West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Troops at Guizhou mutinied and drove out Zhang Congxun. The court named former frontier commissioner Cui Zhuo military governor of Lingnan West.

sentences.zh: 平盧大將王敬武逐節度使安師儒，自爲留後。

translations.literal: Wang Jingwu, a great general of Pinglu, expelled military governor An Shiru and made himself acting military governor.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jingwu, a senior Pinglu general, expelled An Shiru and declared himself acting governor.

sentences.zh: 初，朝廷以龐勳降將湯群爲嵐州刺史，群潛通沙陀，朝廷疑之，徙群懷州刺史，鄭從讜遣使繼告身授之。

translations.literal: Earlier the court had appointed Tang Qun, a surrendered general of Pang Xun, prefect of Lanzhou; Qun secretly communicated with the Shatuo, and the court grew suspicious, transferring him to be prefect of Huaizhou while Zheng Congdang sent envoys in succession to deliver his commission.
translations.idiomatic: The court had earlier made Pang Xun's surrendered general Tang Qun prefect of Lan, but suspected his secret ties to the Shatuo and transferred him to Huai. Zheng Congdang sent envoys to deliver his new commission.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，庚子朔，群殺使者，據城叛，附於沙陀。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on the first day gengzi of the month, Qun killed the envoy, seized the city in rebellion, and joined the Shatuo.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, on the new moon of gengzi, Qun killed the envoy, rebelled, and threw in his lot with the Shatuo.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，從讜遣馬歩都虞候張彥球將兵討之。

translations.literal: On the day renyin, Congdang sent cavalry commander Zhang Yanqiu with troops to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin, Congdang sent cavalry commander Zhang Yanqiu against him.

sentences.zh: 賊帥韓秀升、屈行從起兵，斷峽江路。

translations.literal: The bandit leaders Han Xiusheng and Qu Xingcong raised troops and cut the Yangtze Gorges route.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel leaders Han Xiusheng and Qu Xingcong rose up and blocked traffic on the Three Gorges route.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，陳敬瑄遣押牙莊夢蝶將二千人討之，又遣押牙胡弘略將千人繼之。

translations.literal: On the day guichou, Chen Jingxuan sent adjutant Zhuang Mengdie with two thousand men to attack them, and also sent adjutant Hu Honglue with a thousand men in support.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou, Chen Jingxuan sent adjutant Zhuang Mengdie with two thousand men, followed by Hu Honglue with a thousand more.

sentences.zh: 韓簡復引兵擊鄆州，節度使曹存實逆戰，敗死。

translations.literal: Han Jian again led troops to attack Yanzhou; military governor Cao Cunshi met him in battle, was defeated, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Han Jian attacked Yanzhou again. Governor Cao Cunshi met him in battle, was defeated, and killed.

sentences.zh: 天平都將下邑朱瑄收餘眾，嬰城拒守，簡攻之不下。

translations.literal: Zhu Xuan, a Tianping commander from Xiayi, gathered the survivors, held the city in a tight defense, and Jian could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xuan, a Tianping officer from Xiayi, rallied the survivors, shut the gates, and held out against Jian's assault.

sentences.zh: 詔以瑄權知天平留後。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Xuan acting military governor of Tianping.
translations.idiomatic: The court named Zhu Xuan acting governor of Tianping.

sentences.zh: 以朱溫爲右金吾大將軍、河中行營招討副使，賜名全忠。

translations.literal: Zhu Wen was appointed right Golden Crow general and deputy campaign commander of the Hezhong field headquarters, and granted the name Quanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Wen was made right Golden Crow general and deputy campaign commander for Hezhong, and given the name Quanzhong ('wholly loyal').

sentences.zh: 李克用雖累表請降，而據忻、代州，數侵掠並、汾，爭樓煩監。

translations.literal: Although Li Keyong repeatedly submitted memorials requesting surrender, he held Xin and Dai prefectures, repeatedly raided Bing and Fen, and contested control of the Loufan salt monopoly.
translations.idiomatic: Though Li Keyong kept petitioning to submit, he held Xin and Dai and repeatedly raided Bing and Fen while fighting for the Loufan salt route.

sentences.zh: 義武節度使王處存與克用世爲婚姻，詔處存諭克用：「若誠心款附，宜且歸朔州俟朝命。

translations.literal: Wang Chucun, military governor of Yiwu, was linked to Keyong by generations of marriage; an edict ordered Chucun to instruct Keyong: "If you sincerely wish to submit, you should first return to Shuozhou and await the court's command.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chucun of Yiwu was linked to Keyong by marriage. The court told Chucun to warn him: "If you mean to submit in good faith, return to Shuozhou and await orders.

sentences.zh: 若暴橫如故，當與河東、大同軍共討之。」

translations.literal: If you remain violent and overbearing as before, we shall join with the Hedong and Datong armies to punish you together."
translations.idiomatic: If you continue your raids, Hedong and Datong will join forces against you."

sentences.zh: 以平盧大將王敬武爲留後。

translations.literal: Wang Jingwu, a great general of Pinglu, was appointed acting military governor.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jingwu of Pinglu was confirmed as acting governor.

sentences.zh: 時諸道兵皆會關中討黃巢，獨平盧不至，王鐸遣都統判官、諫議大夫張濬往説之。

translations.literal: At that time troops from all circuits had gathered in Guanzhong to attack Huang Chao; only Pinglu did not come. Wang Duo sent his supreme command staff officer and remonstrance official Zhang Jun to persuade them.
translations.idiomatic: Every circuit had sent troops to Guanzhong against Huang Chao except Pinglu. Wang Duo sent remonstrance official Zhang Jun to bring them in.

sentences.zh: 敬武已受黃巢官爵，不出迎，濬見敬武，責之曰：「公爲天子籓臣，侮慢詔使，不能事上，何以使下！」

translations.literal: Jingwu had already accepted office and rank from Huang Chao and did not come out to welcome him. When Jun met Jingwu he rebuked him, saying: "You are the Son of Heaven's feudatory minister, yet you insult and slight the imperial envoy—you cannot serve your superiors; how can you command your subordinates!"
translations.idiomatic: Jingwu had already accepted rank from Huang Chao and refused to come out to greet him. Zhang Jun rebuked him: "You are the emperor's vassal, yet you insult his envoy. If you cannot serve your lord, how can you command your men?"

sentences.zh: 敬武愕然，謝之。

translations.literal: Jingwu was startled and apologized.
translations.idiomatic: Jingwu was taken aback and apologized.

sentences.zh: 既宣詔，將士皆不應，濬徐諭之曰：「人生當先曉逆順，次知利害。

translations.literal: After the edict was proclaimed the officers and soldiers did not respond. Jun slowly instructed them: "In life one must first understand what is rebellious and what is loyal, and next understand benefit and harm.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict was read, the troops did not respond. Zhang Jun addressed them calmly: "First know loyalty from rebellion; then know gain from loss.

sentences.zh: 黃巢，前日販鹽虜耳，公等捨累葉天子而臣之，果何利哉！

translations.literal: Huang Chao is only yesterday's salt-smuggling barbarian—if you abandon generations of Son of Heaven to serve him, what profit is there!
translations.idiomatic: Huang Chao was only a salt smuggler yesterday—what do you gain by abandoning generations of emperors to serve him!

sentences.zh: 今天下勤王之師皆集京畿，而淄青獨不至。

translations.literal: Today all the armies rallying to the throne have gathered about the capital, yet Ziqing alone has not come.
translations.idiomatic: Every loyal army in the empire is gathering at the capital, yet Ziqing alone stays away.

sentences.zh: 一旦賊平，天子返正，公等何面目見天下之人乎！

translations.literal: Once the bandits are pacified and the Son of Heaven returns to his proper place, with what face will you meet the people of the realm!
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels are crushed and the emperor restored, how will you face the world!

sentences.zh: 不亟往分功名、取富貴，後悔無及矣！」

translations.literal: If you do not hurry west to share in merit and seize wealth and honor, it will be too late for regret!"
translations.idiomatic: March west now to win glory and riches, or you will regret it forever!"

sentences.zh: 將士皆改容引咎，顧謂敬武曰：「諫議之言是也。」

translations.literal: The officers and soldiers all changed expression and accepted blame, turning to Jingwu and saying: "The remonstrance official speaks rightly."
translations.idiomatic: The troops' faces changed; they admitted their error and told Jingwu: "The remonstrance official is right."

sentences.zh: 敬武即發兵從濬而西。

translations.literal: Jingwu immediately raised troops and followed Jun west.
translations.idiomatic: Jingwu at once mobilized and marched west with Zhang Jun.

sentences.zh: 劉漢宏又遣登高鎭將王鎭將兵七萬屯西陵，錢鏐復夜濟江襲擊，大破之，斬獲萬計，得漢宏補諸將官偽敕二百餘通。

translations.literal: Liu Hanhong again sent Wang Zhen, general of Denggao garrison, with seventy thousand troops to encamp at Xiling. Liu again crossed the river at night in an attack, routed them utterly, killed and captured tens of thousands, and obtained more than two hundred forged commissions Hanhong had issued to his generals.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hanhong sent Wang Zhen of Denggao with seventy thousand men to camp at Xiling again. Qian Liu crossed the river by night, routed them, killed or captured tens of thousands, and seized more than two hundred forged commissions Liu had issued.

sentences.zh: 鎭奔諸暨。

translations.literal: Zhen fled to Zhuji.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhen fled to Zhuji.

sentences.zh: 黃巢兵勢尚強，王重榮患之，謂行營都監楊復光曰：「臣賊則負國，討賊則力不足，奈何？」

translations.literal: Huang Chao's military strength was still formidable; Wang Chongrong was troubled by it and said to campaign director Yang Fuguang: "If I submit to the bandits I betray the state; if I attack the bandits my strength is insufficient—what am I to do?"
translations.idiomatic: Huang Chao was still strong, and Wang Chongrong was at a loss. He told campaign director Yang Fuguang: "If I join the rebels I betray the empire; if I fight them I am too weak. What can I do?"

sentences.zh: 復光曰：「雁門李僕射，驍勇，有強兵，其家尊與吾先人嘗共事相善，彼亦有徇國之志。

translations.literal: Fuguang said: "Vice Marshal Li of Yanmen is fierce and brave and has a strong army. His family's elders once served together with my forebears on good terms, and he too has a will to devote himself to the state.
translations.idiomatic: Fuguang replied: "Li Keyong of Yanmen is a fierce fighter with a powerful army. Our families were allies in an earlier generation, and he too wishes to serve the throne.

sentences.zh: 所以不至者，以與河東結隙耳。

translations.literal: The reason he has not come is that he has formed a rift with Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: The reason he has not appeared is a feud with Hedong.

sentences.zh: 誠以朝旨諭鄭公而召之，必來，來則賊不足平矣！」

translations.literal: If we truly use the court's order to instruct Duke Zheng and summon him, he will certainly come; once he comes, the rebels will not be hard to pacify!"
translations.idiomatic: If His Majesty's orders were conveyed to Duke Zheng to summon him, he would surely come—and once he came, the rebels would be easily defeated."

sentences.zh: 東面宣慰使王徽亦以爲然。

translations.literal: The eastern pacification commissioner Wang Hui also thought so.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern pacification commissioner Wang Hui agreed.

sentences.zh: 時王鐸在河中，乃以墨敕召李克用，諭鄭從讜。

translations.literal: At that time Wang Duo was at Hezhong; he then used an ink edict to summon Li Keyong and instructed Zheng Congdian.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Duo was then at Hezhong; he issued an informal imperial summons for Li Keyong and urged Zheng Congdian to cooperate.

sentences.zh: 十一月，克用將沙陀萬七千自嵐、石路趣河中，不敢入太原境，獨與數百騎過晉陽城下與從讜別，從讜以名馬、器幣贈之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Keyong led seventeen thousand Shatuo troops by the Lan and Shi route toward Hezhong; he dared not enter Taiyuan territory, but alone with several hundred horsemen passed below Jinyang city to take leave of Congdian; Congdian presented him with famous horses, vessels, and gifts.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Li Keyong marched seventeen thousand Shatuo soldiers along the Lan–Shi road toward Hezhong. He would not enter Taiyuan's jurisdiction; with only a few hundred riders he passed beneath Jinyang to bid Zheng Congdian farewell, and Congdian sent him off with fine horses and gifts.

sentences.zh: 李詳舊卒共逐黃思鄴，推華陰鎭使王遇爲主，以華州降於王重榮，王鐸承製以遇爲刺史。

translations.literal: The old soldiers of Li Xiang together drove out Huang Siye, made Wang Yu, commissioner of Huayin garrison, their leader, and surrendered Hua prefecture to Wang Chongrong; Wang Duo by imperial commission made Yu prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiang's former troops expelled Huang Siye and set up Huayin garrison commissioner Wang Yu as their leader, surrendering Hua prefecture to Wang Chongrong; Wang Duo appointed Yu prefect by imperial commission.

sentences.zh: 阡能黨愈熾，侵淫入蜀州境。

translations.literal: Qian Neng's faction grew ever fiercer, encroaching into Shu prefecture's territory.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Neng's followers grew bolder still, pushing into the borders of Shu prefecture.

sentences.zh: 陳敬瑄以楊行遷等久無功，以押牙高仁厚爲都招討指揮使，將兵五百人往代之。

translations.literal: Chen Jingxuan, because Yang Xingqian and others had long achieved nothing, appointed his tooth-guard Gao Renhou as overall campaign commander and sent five hundred troops to replace them.
translations.idiomatic: Because Yang Xingqian and others had failed for so long, Chen Jingxuan named his adjutant Gao Renhou overall pacification commander and sent five hundred men to relieve them.

sentences.zh: 未發前一日，有鬻面者，自旦至午，出入營中數四，邏者疑之，執而訊之，果阡能之諜也。

translations.literal: On the day before they set out, a noodle-seller from dawn till noon entered and left the camp four or five times; patrols grew suspicious, seized and questioned him—it proved to be Qian Neng's spy.
translations.idiomatic: The day before departure, a man selling noodles passed in and out of camp repeatedly from dawn until noon. Patrols grew suspicious, seized him, and under questioning he proved to be Qian Neng's spy.

sentences.zh: 仁厚命釋縛，溫言問之，對曰：「某村民，阡能囚其父母妻子於獄，云『汝詗事歸，得實則免汝家；

translations.literal: Renhou ordered his bonds cut and questioned him gently. He replied, 'I am a villager. Qian Neng imprisoned my parents, wife, and children and said, "You go spy and return; if what you report is true we will spare your household;
translations.idiomatic: Renhou had his bonds removed and questioned him kindly. The man answered, 'I am a common villager. Qian Neng threw my parents, wife, and children into prison and told me, "Go spy on the army and come back. If your report is true, your family goes free;

sentences.zh: 不然，盡死！』

translations.literal: Otherwise, all will die!'
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise the whole household dies!'

sentences.zh: 某非願爾也。」

translations.literal: I did not wish it so.'
translations.idiomatic: I never wanted to do this.'

sentences.zh: 仁厚曰：「誠知汝如是，我何忍殺汝！

translations.literal: Renhou said, 'Knowing truly that it is as you say, how could I bear to kill you!
translations.idiomatic: Renhou said, 'Now that I know your story, how could I bring myself to kill you!

sentences.zh: 今縱汝歸，救汝父母妻子，但語阡能云：『高尚書來日發，所將止五百人，無多兵也。』

translations.literal: Now I release you to return and save your parents, wife, and children; only tell Qian Neng: "Vice Minister Gao sets out tomorrow; he brings only five hundred men—no great force."
translations.idiomatic: I will let you go home to your family. Only tell Qian Neng this: "Minister Gao marches tomorrow with just five hundred men—hardly a large host."

sentences.zh: 然我活汝一家，汝當爲我潛語寨中人云：『僕射愍汝曹皆良人，爲賊所制，情非得已。

translations.literal: Yet because I spare your whole household, you must secretly tell those in the stockades for me: "The prefect pities you all as good people compelled by the bandits, not of your own will.
translations.idiomatic: But because I have spared your household, secretly tell everyone in the camps: "The Vice Minister knows you are honest folk forced into rebellion against your will.

sentences.zh: 尚書欲拯救湔洗汝曹，尚書來，汝曹各投兵迎降。

translations.literal: The minister intends to rescue and cleanse you; when the minister comes, each of you cast aside weapons and welcome surrender.
translations.idiomatic: He means to save and restore you. When he arrives, throw down your arms and surrender.

sentences.zh: 尚書當使人書汝背爲「歸順」字，遣汝復舊業。

translations.literal: The minister will have men write the characters 'submitted in allegiance' on your backs and send you back to your former occupations.
translations.idiomatic: He will mark your backs with the word 'Surrendered' and send you home to your old livelihoods.

sentences.zh: 所欲誅者，阡能、羅渾擎、句胡僧、羅夫子、韓求五人耳，必不使橫及百姓也。』」

translations.literal: Those he means to execute are only the five: Qian Neng, Luo Hunqing, Gou Huseng, Luo Fuzi, and Han Qiu—he will certainly not let harm spread to the common people.'"
translations.idiomatic: Only five men will die: Qian Neng, Luo Hunqing, Gou Huseng, Luo Fuzi, and Han Qiu. No harm will come to ordinary people.'"

sentences.zh: 諜曰：「此皆百姓心上事，尚書盡知而赦之，其誰不舞躍聽命！

translations.literal: The spy said, 'These are exactly what the people desire in their hearts; if the minister knows all this and pardons them, who would not leap for joy and obey!
translations.idiomatic: The spy said, 'That is everything the people long for. Once they know the Minister pardons them, who will not leap to obey!

sentences.zh: 一口傳百，百傳千，川騰海沸，不可遏也。

translations.literal: One mouth passes to a hundred, a hundred to a thousand—like rivers surging and seas boiling, it cannot be stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Word will spread one to a hundred, a hundred to a thousand—like rivers in flood and seas in storm, nothing can hold it back.

sentences.zh: 比尚書之至，百姓必盡奔赴如嬰兒之見慈母，阡能孤居，立成擒矣！」

translations.literal: By the time the minister arrives, the people will surely all rush to him as infants to a loving mother; Qian Neng left alone will be captured at once!'
translations.idiomatic: When the Minister arrives, the people will flock to him as children to a mother. Qian Neng, left alone, will be seized in an instant!'

sentences.zh: 遂遣之。

translations.literal: He was sent off.
translations.idiomatic: Renhou sent him on his way.

sentences.zh: 明日，仁厚引兵發，至雙流，把截使白文現出迎。

translations.literal: The next day Renhou led his troops forth; reaching Shuangliu, the interception commissioner Bai Wenxian came out to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Renhou marched out and reached Shuangliu, where interception commissioner Bai Wenxian came out to greet him.

sentences.zh: 仁厚周視塹柵，怒曰：「阡能役夫，其眾皆耕民耳，竭一府之兵，歲餘不能擒，今觀塹柵重複牢密如此，宜其可認安眠飽食，養寇邀功也！」

translations.literal: Renhou surveyed ditches and palisades all around and said angrily, 'Qian Neng's laborers—all his followers are plowmen; exhausting one prefecture's troops for more than a year they could not capture him; now seeing ditches and palisades layered and secure like this, no wonder they could sleep soundly, eat their fill, nurture the bandits and seek merit!'
translations.idiomatic: Renhou inspected the trenches and palisades and burst out in anger: 'Qian Neng's men are farmers! The whole prefecture exhausted its army for more than a year and could not catch him—and with fortifications this elaborate, no wonder you could sleep well, eat heartily, and fatten the rebels to win glory!'

sentences.zh: 命引出斬之。

translations.literal: He ordered him brought out and beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Bai Wenxian dragged out for execution.

sentences.zh: 監軍力救，久之，乃得免。

translations.literal: The army supervisor strove to save him; after long effort he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: The supervising commissioner pleaded hard for him, and after a long dispute Bai was spared.

sentences.zh: 命悉平塹柵，才留五百兵守之，餘兵悉以自隨，又召諸寨兵，相繼皆集。

translations.literal: He ordered all ditches and palisades leveled, retaining only five hundred soldiers to garrison them; all remaining troops he took with him, and summoned garrison troops from the various stockades—they came in succession and gathered.
translations.idiomatic: He had every trench and palisade torn down, left only five hundred men to hold the post, and took the rest with him. He also called up troops from the other camps, who came flocking in.

sentences.zh: 阡能聞仁厚將至，遣羅渾擎立五寨於雙流之西，伏兵千人於野橋箐以邀官軍。

translations.literal: Learning Renhou was coming, Qian Neng sent Luo Hunqing to establish five stockades west of Shuangliu and stationed a thousand ambush troops at Yeqiao Ravine to intercept the government army.
translations.idiomatic: When Qian Neng heard Renhou was approaching, he sent Luo Hunqing to build five camps west of Shuangliu and posted a thousand men in ambush at Yeqiao Ravine to intercept the government forces.

sentences.zh: 仁厚詗知，引兵圍之，下令勿殺，遣人釋戎服賊中告諭，如昨日所以語諜者。

translations.literal: Renhou learned of it, led troops to surround them, ordered no killing, and sent men stripped of battle dress among the rebels to proclaim as he had told the spy yesterday.
translations.idiomatic: Renhou learned of the ambush, surrounded the camps, forbade killing, and sent unarmed men among the rebels to repeat the message he had given the spy.

sentences.zh: 賊大喜，呼噪，爭棄甲投兵請降，拜如摧山。

translations.literal: The rebels were greatly pleased, shouted and clamored, vied to cast off armor and throw down weapons begging to surrender, bowing as if mountains were collapsing.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels rejoiced, shouting and cheering; they threw off armor and weapons and begged to surrender, kowtowing in waves like an avalanche.

sentences.zh: 仁厚悉撫諭，書其背，使歸語寨中未降者，寨中餘眾爭出降。

translations.literal: Renhou comforted and instructed them all, wrote on their backs, had them return to speak to those in stockades who had not surrendered—the remaining masses in the stockades vied to come out and surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Renhou reassured them all, marked their backs, and sent them to tell the holdouts in other camps. Those camps too poured out to surrender.

sentences.zh: 渾擎狼狽逾塹走，其眾執以詣仁厚，仁厚曰：「此愚夫，不足與語。」

translations.literal: Hunqing fled in panic over the ditch; his men seized him and brought him to Renhou. Renhou said, 'This foolish fellow is not worth speaking with.'
translations.idiomatic: Luo Hunqing scrambled over the palisade and fled, but his own men seized him and brought him to Renhou, who said, 'This fool is not worth addressing.'

sentences.zh: 械以送府。

translations.literal: He was shackled and sent to headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: They put him in chains and sent him to headquarters.

sentences.zh: 悉命焚五寨及其甲兵，惟留旗幟，所降凡四千人。

translations.literal: He ordered all five stockades and their armor and weapons burned, keeping only banners; those who surrendered numbered four thousand in all.
translations.idiomatic: He burned all five camps along with their arms and armor, keeping only the banners. Four thousand men surrendered in all.

sentences.zh: 明旦，仁厚謂降者曰：「始欲即遣汝歸，而前塗諸寨百姓未知吾心，或有憂疑，藉汝曹爲我前行，過穿口、新津寨下，示以背字告諭之，比至延貢，可歸矣。」

translations.literal: Next morning Renhou said to the surrenderers, 'At first I wished to send you back at once, but along the road the people in the various stockades do not yet know my mind and may harbor doubts; I rely on you to go ahead for me. Passing beneath the stockades at Chuankou and Xinjin, show the characters on your backs and proclaim—by the time you reach Yangong you may return.'
translations.idiomatic: The next morning Renhou told the prisoners, 'I meant to send you home at once, but the people along the road do not yet know my intentions and may hesitate. Go ahead of me. Pass Chuankou and Xinjin, show the marks on your backs, and spread the word. By the time you reach Yangong you may go home.'

sentences.zh: 乃取渾擎旗倒系之，每五十人爲隊，授以一旗，使前走，揚旗疾呼曰：「羅渾擎已生擒，送使府，大軍行至。

translations.literal: He then took Hunqing's banners and hung them upside down; every fifty men formed a squad, each given a banner to run ahead, waving the banners and crying swiftly: 'Luo Hunqing has been captured alive and sent to headquarters; the great army is marching.
translations.idiomatic: He took Luo Hunqing's banners, hung them upside down, and formed the men into squads of fifty, each with a flag. They ran ahead shouting, 'Luo Hunqing is taken alive and sent to headquarters! The main army is coming!

sentences.zh: 汝曹居寨中者，速如我出降，立得爲良人，無事矣！」

translations.literal: You who dwell in stockades, quickly surrender as we have and at once become good people—no trouble!'
translations.idiomatic: Everyone still in the camps—surrender now as we did, and you will be free and safe at once!'

sentences.zh: 至穿口，句胡僧置十一寨，寨中人爭出降。

translations.literal: Reaching Chuankou, Gou Huseng had established eleven stockades; those in the stockades vied to come out and surrender.
translations.idiomatic: At Chuankou, where Gou Huseng had eleven camps, the inhabitants rushed out to surrender.

sentences.zh: 胡僧大驚，拔劍遏之，眾投瓦石擊之，共擒以獻仁厚，其眾五千餘皆降。

translations.literal: Huseng was greatly alarmed, drew his sword to restrain them; the crowd threw tiles and stones at him, together seized him and presented him to Renhou; his followers, more than five thousand, all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Gou Huseng panicked and tried to stop them with his sword. The crowd pelted him with stones, seized him, and delivered him to Renhou. More than five thousand of his men surrendered.

sentences.zh: 又明旦，焚寨，使降者執旗先驅，一如雙流。

translations.literal: Again the next morning they burned the stockades and had the surrenderers carry banners as vanguard, just as at Shuangliu.
translations.idiomatic: The following morning they burned the camps and sent the surrenderers ahead with flags, just as at Shuangliu.

sentences.zh: 至新津，韓求置十三寨皆迎降。

translations.literal: Reaching Xinjin, Han Qiu's thirteen stockades all welcomed surrender.
translations.idiomatic: At Xinjin all thirteen of Han Qiu's camps submitted without a fight.

sentences.zh: 求自投深塹，其眾鉤出之，已死，斬首以獻。

translations.literal: Qiu threw himself into a deep ditch; his men hooked him out—already dead—and presented his severed head.
translations.idiomatic: Han Qiu threw himself into a deep trench; his men pulled him out dead and presented his head.

sentences.zh: 將士欲焚寨，仁厚止之曰：「降人皆未食。」

translations.literal: The officers and soldiers wished to burn the stockades; Renhou stopped them, saying, 'The surrenderers have all gone without food.'
translations.idiomatic: The troops wanted to burn the camps, but Renhou stopped them: 'The surrenderers have not eaten.'

sentences.zh: 使先運出資糧，然後焚之。

translations.literal: He had provisions carried out first, then burned them.
translations.idiomatic: He had supplies brought out first, then set the camps ablaze.

sentences.zh: 新降者競炊爨，與先降來告者共食之，語笑歌吹，終夜不絶。

translations.literal: The newly surrendered vied to cook; they ate together with those who had surrendered earlier and come to report, talking, laughing, singing, and playing music without cease all night.
translations.idiomatic: The new prisoners rushed to cook; they shared food with the earlier surrenderers who had come ahead, laughing, talking, singing, and playing music through the night.

sentences.zh: 明日，仁厚縱雙流，穿口降者先歸，使新津降者執旗前驅，且曰：「入邛州境，亦可散歸矣。」

translations.literal: The next day Renhou released the Shuangliu and Chuankou surrenderers to return first, had the Xinjin surrenderers carry banners as vanguard, and said, 'When you enter Qiong prefecture's territory you may also scatter and return.'
translations.idiomatic: The next day Renhou let the men from Shuangliu and Chuankou go home first and sent the Xinjin prisoners ahead with flags, telling them they could disperse once they entered Qiong prefecture.

sentences.zh: 羅夫子置九寨於延貢，其眾前夕望新津火光，已不眠矣。

translations.literal: Luo Fuzi had established nine stockades at Yangong; his followers the night before had seen Xinjin's fires and already could not sleep.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Fuzi held nine camps at Yangong. The night before, his men had seen the fires at Xinjin and could not sleep.

sentences.zh: 及新津人至，羅夫子脫身棄寨奔阡能，其眾皆降。

translations.literal: When the Xinjin men arrived, Luo Fuzi slipped away, abandoned his stockades, and fled to Qian Neng; his followers all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xinjin prisoners arrived, Luo Fuzi abandoned his camps and fled to Qian Neng. His entire force surrendered.

sentences.zh: 明日，羅夫子至阡能寨，與之謀悉眾決戰。

translations.literal: The next day Luo Fuzi reached Qian Neng's stockade and with him plotted to muster all forces for a decisive battle.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Luo Fuzi reached Qian Neng's camp and urged a last stand with every man they had.

sentences.zh: 計未定，日向暮，延貢降者至，阡能、羅夫子走馬巡寨，欲出兵，眾皆不應。

translations.literal: The plan was not settled when the day turned toward dusk; the Yangong surrenderers arrived; Qian Neng and Luo Fuzi rode horses touring the stockades wishing to send out troops—the crowd would not respond.
translations.idiomatic: Before they could decide, dusk fell and the Yangong surrenderers arrived. Qian Neng and Luo Fuzi rode through the camps calling for battle, but no one answered.

sentences.zh: 仁厚引兵連夜逼之，明旦，諸寨知大軍已近，呼噪爭出，執阡能，阡能窘急赴井，爲眾所擒，不死；

translations.literal: Renhou led troops pressing them through the night; at dawn the stockades knew the great army was near, shouted and clamored vying to come out, seized Qian Neng—Qian Neng in distress rushed toward a well, was seized by the crowd, not dead;
translations.idiomatic: Renhou pressed forward through the night. At dawn the camps knew the main force was near. Men poured out shouting, seized Qian Neng, who in desperation ran for a well but was caught alive;

sentences.zh: 又執羅夫子，羅夫子自剄。

translations.literal: They also seized Luo Fuzi; Luo Fuzi cut his own throat.
translations.idiomatic: They seized Luo Fuzi as well, but he slit his own throat.

sentences.zh: 眾挈羅夫子首，縛阡能，驅之前迎官，見仁厚，擁馬首大呼泣拜曰：「百姓負冤日久，無所控訴。

translations.literal: The crowd carrying Luo Fuzi's head, bound Qian Neng, drove them forward to meet the officials; seeing Renhou, they embraced his horse's head, cried out weeping and kowtowed, saying, 'The people have borne injustice long with nowhere to appeal.
translations.idiomatic: Carrying Luo Fuzi's head and Qian Neng bound, they rushed to meet the army. When they saw Renhou they clung to his horse's bridle, weeping and kowtowing, and cried, 'We have suffered wrongs for so long with nowhere to turn.

sentences.zh: 自諜者還，百姓引領，度頃刻如期年。

translations.literal: Since the spy returned, the people craned their necks, measuring moments like years.
translations.idiomatic: From the day the spy came back we have waited, necks stretched, each hour feeling like a year.

sentences.zh: 今遇尚書，如出九泉睹白日，已死而復生矣！」

translations.literal: Now meeting the minister is like emerging from the nine springs to behold the white sun—dead and alive again!'
translations.idiomatic: To meet the Minister is like rising from the grave into daylight—we are dead men brought back to life!'

sentences.zh: 歡呼不可止。

translations.literal: Shouts of joy could not be stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Their cheers would not cease.

sentences.zh: 賊寨在他所者，分遣諸將往降之。

translations.literal: Stockades of rebels elsewhere he dispatched various generals to go and accept their surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Renhou sent his generals to accept surrenders from rebel camps elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 仁厚出軍凡六日，五賊皆平。

translations.literal: Renhou had been on campaign only six days in all; the five bandit leaders were all pacified.
translations.idiomatic: In only six days on campaign Renhou had crushed all five rebel leaders.

sentences.zh: 每下縣鎭，輒補鎭遏使，使安集戸口。

translations.literal: Whenever he took a county or market-town, he would appoint a garrison controller to settle household registers.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he took a county or market town, he appointed a pacification officer to restore the population registers.

sentences.zh: 於是陳敬瑄梟韓求、羅夫子首於市，釘阡能、羅渾擎、句胡僧於城西，七日而冎之。

translations.literal: Thereupon Chen Jingxuan displayed Han Qiu's and Luo Fuzi's heads in the market; nailed Qian Neng, Luo Hunqing, and Gou Huseng at the city's west wall; after seven days dismembered them.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jingxuan then exposed Han Qiu's and Luo Fuzi's heads in the marketplace, nailed Qian Neng, Luo Hunqing, and Gou Huseng to the west wall of the city, and after seven days dismembered their bodies.

sentences.zh: 阡能孔目官張榮，本安仁進士，屢舉不中第，歸於阡能，爲之謀主，爲草書檄；

translations.literal: Qian Neng's clerical officer Zhang Rong was originally a Jinshi from Anren, repeatedly failed the examinations, returned to Qian Neng, became his strategist, and drafted proclamations;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Rong, Qian Neng's chief clerk, was a native of Anren who had repeatedly failed the civil examinations and joined Qian Neng as his strategist, drafting his proclamations;

sentences.zh: 阡能敗，以詩啟求哀於仁厚，仁厚送府，釘於馬市。

translations.literal: When Qian Neng was defeated, he submitted a poem pleading for mercy to Renhou; Renhou sent him to headquarters; he was nailed at the horse market.
translations.idiomatic: When Qian Neng fell, Zhang Rong sent Renhou a poem begging for his life. Renhou forwarded him to headquarters, where he was impaled at the horse market.

sentences.zh: 自餘不戮一人。

translations.literal: Beyond that not one person was executed.
translations.idiomatic: No one else was put to death.

sentences.zh: 十二月，以仁厚爲眉州防禦使。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Renhou was made defender of Meizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Gao Renhou was appointed defender of Meizhou.

sentences.zh: 陳敬瑄榜邛州，凡阡能等親黨皆不問。

translations.literal: Chen Jingxuan posted a notice in Qiong prefecture that all close kin of Qian Neng and the rest would not be prosecuted.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jingxuan posted a proclamation in Qiong prefecture granting amnesty to all relatives and associates of Qian Neng and his followers.

sentences.zh: 未幾，邛州刺史申捕獲阡能叔父行全家三十五人繫獄，請准法。

translations.literal: Before long the prefect of Qiong Shen Bu captured Qian Neng's uncle Xing Quan's entire household of thirty-five persons and imprisoned them, requesting application of the law.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the prefect of Qiong, Shen Bu, arrested thirty-five members of Qian Neng's uncle Xing Quan's household and imprisoned them, asking that the law be applied.

sentences.zh: 敬瑄以問孔目官唐溪，對曰：「公已有榜，令勿問，而刺史復捕之，此必有故。

translations.literal: Jingxuan asked his clerical officer Tang Xi, who answered, 'Your Excellency already had a notice ordering no inquiry, yet the prefect again arrests them—there must be a reason.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jingxuan consulted his clerk Tang Xi, who replied, 'Your Excellency has already promised not to prosecute them, yet the prefect arrests them again. There must be an ulterior motive.

sentences.zh: 今若殺之，豈惟使明公失大信，竊恐阡能之黨紛紛復起矣！」

translations.literal: If they are killed now, not only will Your Excellency lose great trust—I fear Qian Neng's faction will rise again in droves!'
translations.idiomatic: If you execute them now, you will not only break your word—I fear Qian Neng's followers will rise up all over again!'

sentences.zh: 敬瑄從之，遣押牙牛暈往，集眾於州門，破械而釋之，因詢其所以然。

translations.literal: Jingxuan followed this, dispatched his tooth-guard Niu Yun, assembled the crowd at the prefectural gate, broke their shackles and released them, and inquired the reason.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jingxuan agreed. He sent his adjutant Niu Yun to the prefectural gate, gathered the crowd, broke their chains, freed them, and asked why they had been seized.

sentences.zh: 果行全有良田，刺史欲買之，不與，故恨之。

translations.literal: Indeed Xing Quan had fertile fields; the prefect wished to buy them and he would not yield, hence the grudge.
translations.idiomatic: It turned out Xing Quan owned rich farmland that the prefect had tried to buy; Xing Quan refused, and the prefect bore a grudge.

sentences.zh: 敬瑄召刺史，將按其罪，刺史以憂死。

translations.literal: Jingxuan summoned the prefect intending to investigate his crime; the prefect died from anxiety.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jingxuan summoned the prefect to answer for his crime, but the man died of fright before he could be tried.

sentences.zh: 他日，行全聞其家由唐溪以免，密餉溪蝕箔金百兩。

translations.literal: Another day Xing Quan heard his family had been spared through Tang Xi and secretly presented Xi with a hundred taels of gold foil.
translations.idiomatic: Later Xing Quan learned his family had been saved through Tang Xi and secretly sent him a hundred taels of gold leaf as a gift.

sentences.zh: 溪怒曰：「此乃太師仁明，何預吾事，汝乃懷禍相餉乎！」

translations.literal: Xi angrily said, 'This was the Grand Preceptor's benevolence and clarity—what has it to do with me? Do you bring mischief in your gift?'
translations.idiomatic: Tang Xi flew into a rage: 'That was the Grand Preceptor's mercy, not mine. Are you trying to buy me with this bribe?'

sentences.zh: 還其金，斥逐使去。

translations.literal: He returned the gold and drove the messenger away.
translations.idiomatic: He returned the gold and had the messenger driven off.

sentences.zh: 河東節度使鄭從讜奏克嵐州，執湯群，斬之。

translations.literal: Hedong military governor Zheng Congdian memorialized that Lan prefecture had been taken, Tang Qun seized and beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Hedong military governor Zheng Congdian reported the capture of Lan prefecture, the seizure of Tang Qun, and his execution.

sentences.zh: 以忻、代等州留後李克用爲雁門節度使。

translations.literal: Li Keyong, regent of Xin, Dai, and other prefectures, was made military governor of Yanmen.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong, acting commissioner of Xin, Dai, and related prefectures, was appointed military governor of Yanmen.

sentences.zh: 初，朝廷以鄭紹業爲荊南節度使，時段彥謨方據荊南，紹業憚之，逾半歲，乃至鎭。

translations.literal: Initially the court appointed Zheng Shaoye military governor of Jingnan; at that time Duan Yanmo held Jingnan; Shaoye feared him; after more than half a year he finally reached his post.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the court had named Zheng Shaoye military governor of Jingnan, but Duan Yanmo already held the region. Shaoye was afraid of him and did not reach his post for more than half a year.

sentences.zh: 上幸蜀，召紹業還，以彥謨爲節度使。

translations.literal: The emperor went to Shu, recalled Shaoye, and made Yanmo military governor.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor fled to Shu, Shaoye was recalled and Duan Yanmo was made military governor.

sentences.zh: 彥謨爲朱敬玫所殺，復以紹業爲節度使。

translations.literal: Yanmo was killed by Zhu Jingmei; Shaoye was again made military governor.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Yanmo was killed by Zhu Jingmei, and Zheng Shaoye was appointed military governor again.

sentences.zh: 紹業畏敬玫，逗遛不進，軍中久無帥，至是，敬玫署押牙陳儒知府事。

translations.literal: Shaoye feared Jingmei and lingered without advancing; the army long lacked a commander; at this time Jingmei commissioned his tooth-guard Chen Ru to manage prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoye feared Zhu Jingmei and hung back. The army had been without a commander for a long time, and now Zhu Jingmei put his adjutant Chen Ru in charge of the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 儒，江陵人也。

translations.literal: Ru was a man of Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Ru was a native of Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 加奉天節度使齊克儉、河中節度使王重榮並同平章事。

translations.literal: Fengtian military governor Qi Kejian and Hezhong military governor Wang Chongrong were both promoted to co-director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Fengtian military governor Qi Kejian and Hezhong military governor Wang Chongrong were both made honorary chancellors.

sentences.zh: 李克用將兵四萬至河中，遣從父弟克修先將兵五百濟河嘗賊。

translations.literal: Li Keyong led forty thousand troops to Hezhong and sent his father's younger cousin Kexiu ahead with five hundred men to cross the river and test the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong marched forty thousand men to Hezhong and sent his cousin Li Kexiu ahead with five hundred troops to cross the Yellow River and probe the rebel lines.

sentences.zh: 初，克用弟克讓爲南山寺僧所殺，其僕渾進通歸於黃巢。

translations.literal: Initially Keyong's brother Kerang had been killed by monks of Nanshan Temple; his servant Hun Jintong went over to Huang Chao.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Keyong's brother Li Kerang had been killed by monks of Nanshan Temple, and Kerang's servant Hun Jintong had joined Huang Chao.

sentences.zh: 自高潯之敗，諸軍皆畏賊，莫敢進。

translations.literal: Since Gao Xun's defeat all armies feared the rebels and none dared advance.
translations.idiomatic: After Gao Xun's defeat every government army feared the rebels and dared not advance.

sentences.zh: 及克用軍至，賊憚之，曰：「鴉軍至矣，當避其鋒。」

translations.literal: When Keyong's army arrived the rebels feared them and said, 'The Crow Army has come—we should avoid their edge.'
translations.idiomatic: When Li Keyong's forces arrived, the rebels were afraid and said, 'The Crow Army is here. We must avoid their edge.'

sentences.zh: 克用軍皆衣黑，故謂之鴉軍。

translations.literal: Keyong's troops all wore black, hence they were called the Crow Army.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong's soldiers all wore black, which is why they were called the Crow Army.

sentences.zh: 巢乃捕南山寺僧十餘人，遣使繼詔書及重賂，因渾進通詣克用以求和。

translations.literal: Chao then seized more than ten monks of Nanshan Temple, sent envoys with successive edicts and heavy bribes, and through Hun Jintong went to Keyong to seek peace.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Chao seized more than a dozen monks from Nanshan Temple, sent envoys bearing imperial edicts and rich gifts, and dispatched Hun Jintong to Li Keyong to sue for peace.

sentences.zh: 克用殺僧，哭克讓，受其賂以分諸將，焚其詔書，歸其使者，引兵自夏陽渡河，軍於同州。

translations.literal: Keyong killed the monks, wept for Kerang, accepted the bribes and divided them among the generals, burned their edicts, sent back their envoys, led troops from Xiayang across the river, and encamped at Tong prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong executed the monks, mourned his brother, took the bribes and divided them among his officers, burned Huang Chao's edicts, sent the envoys back, crossed the river from Xiayang, and encamped at Tong prefecture.

sentences.zh: 孟方立既殺成麟，引兵歸邢州，潞人請監軍呉全勖知留後。

translations.literal: Meng Fangli having killed Cheng Lin, led troops back to Xing prefecture; the people of Lu requested the army supervisor Wu Quanxun as regent.
translations.idiomatic: After Meng Fangli killed Cheng Lin and withdrew to Xingzhou, the people of Lu asked that army supervisor Wu Quanxun be made acting commissioner.

sentences.zh: 是歲，王鐸墨制以方立知邢州事，方立不受，囚全勖；

translations.literal: That year Wang Duo by ink edict made Fangli regent of Xing prefecture affairs; Fangli did not accept and imprisoned Quanxun;
translations.idiomatic: That year Wang Duo appointed Meng Fangli acting commissioner of Xingzhou by informal edict, but Fangli refused and imprisoned Wu Quanxun;

sentences.zh: 與鐸書，願得儒臣鎭潞州，鐸以鄭昌圖知昭義軍事。

translations.literal: he wrote Duo wishing to obtain a Confucian minister to govern Lu prefecture; Duo appointed Zheng Changtu to manage Zhaoyi military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote to Wang Duo asking for a scholar-official to govern Luzhou, and Duo put Zheng Changtu in charge of Zhaoyi affairs.

sentences.zh: 既而朝廷以右僕射、租庸使王徽同平章事，充昭義節度使，徽以車駕播遷，中原方擾，方立專據山東邢、洺、磁三州，度朝廷力未能制，辭不行，請且委昌圖。

translations.literal: Soon after the court made Right Vice Director and Transport Commissioner Wang Hui co-director and military governor of Zhaoyi; Hui because the imperial carriage was in flight and the central plain was in turmoil, Fangli solely held Xing, Ming, and Ci of eastern Shandong, judged the court's strength could not control him, declined to go, and asked to leave affairs temporarily to Changtu.
translations.idiomatic: The court then named Right Vice Director and transport commissioner Wang Hui chancellor and military governor of Zhaoyi. Wang Hui saw the emperor in exile and the central plains in chaos; Meng Fangli held Xing, Ming, and Ci in eastern Shandong and seemed beyond the court's reach. Wang declined the post and asked that affairs remain with Zheng Changtu for the time being.

sentences.zh: 詔以徽爲大明宮留守、京畿安撫制置修奉園陵使。

translations.literal: An edict made Hui Grand Palace custodian and capital-district pacification commissioner for preparing and repairing the imperial tombs.
translations.idiomatic: An edict instead made Wang Hui custodian of the Daming Palace and commissioner for pacifying the capital region and restoring the imperial tombs.

sentences.zh: 昌圖至潞州，不三月而去，方立遂遷昭義軍於邢州，自稱留後，表其將李殷銳爲潞州刺史。

translations.literal: Changtu reached Lu prefecture and within three months departed; Fangli then moved the Zhaoyi army to Xing prefecture, styled himself regent, and memorialized his general Li Yinrui as prefect of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Changtu reached Luzhou but left within three months. Meng Fangli then moved the Zhaoyi headquarters to Xingzhou, styled himself acting commissioner, and recommended his general Li Yinrui as prefect of Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 和州刺史秦彥使其子將兵數千襲宣州，逐觀察使竇潏而代之。

translations.literal: He prefectural governor Qin Yan sent his son with several thousand troops to raid Xuan prefecture, drove out observation commissioner Dou Yu and replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Yan, prefect of Hezhou, sent his son with several thousand troops to attack Xuanzhou, expelled observation commissioner Dou Yu, and took his place.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，李克用將李存貞敗黃揆於沙苑；

translations.literal: Spring, first month: Li Keyong's general Li Cunzhen defeated Huang Kui at Shayuan;
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, Li Keyong's general Li Cunzhen defeated Huang Kui at Shayuan.

sentences.zh: 己巳，克用進屯沙苑。

translations.literal: On the day jisi Keyong advanced and encamped at Shayuan.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jisi Li Keyong advanced and encamped at Shayuan.

sentences.zh: 揆，巢之弟也。

translations.literal: Kui was Chao's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Kui was Huang Chao's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 王鐸承製以克用爲東北面行營都統，以楊復光爲東面都統監軍使，陳景思爲北面都統監軍使。

translations.literal: Wang Duo by imperial commission made Keyong overall commander of the northeast campaign army, Yang Fuguang eastern overall army supervisor, and Chen Jingsi northern overall army supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Duo appointed Li Keyong supreme commander of the northeastern campaign army, Yang Fuguang eastern army supervisor, and Chen Jingsi northern army supervisor by imperial commission.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，制以中書令、充諸道行營都統王鐸爲義成節度使，令赴鎭。

translations.literal: On the day yihai, by edict Wang Duo, Grand Councilor and overall commander of the all-circuits campaign army, was made Yicheng military commissioner and ordered to go to his post.
translations.idiomatic: On the day yihai, an edict appointed Wang Duo, Grand Councilor and supreme commander of the multi-circuit campaign army, military commissioner of Yicheng and ordered him to take up the post.

sentences.zh: 田令孜欲歸重北司，稱鐸討黃巢久無功，卒用楊復光策，召沙陀而破之，故罷鐸兵柄以悅復光。

translations.literal: Tian Lingzi wished to return weight to the northern offices, saying Duo long had no achievement campaigning against Huang Chao; in the end Yang Fuguang's plan was used, calling the Shatuo and breaking them, therefore Duo's military authority was removed to please Fuguang.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Lingzi wanted to shift power back to the eunuch directorates. He claimed Wang Duo had achieved nothing after long campaigning against Huang Chao, and that the court had finally adopted Yang Fuguang's plan of summoning the Shatuo, who then broke the rebels. Duo's command was therefore stripped to gratify Fuguang.

sentences.zh: 又以副都統崔安潛爲東都留守，以都都監西門思恭爲右神策中尉，充諸道租庸兼催促諸道進軍等使。

translations.literal: Again, deputy overall commander Cui Anqian was made eastern capital defender; overall army overseer Ximen Sigong was made right Shence army commander, also filling envoy for all-circuits land tax and urging all circuits to advance armies.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Anqian, the deputy supreme commander, was appointed defender of the eastern capital, and Ximen Sigong, the chief army overseer, was made commander of the Right Shence Army and commissioned as envoy for circuit land taxes and for pressing all circuits to march their troops forward.

sentences.zh: 令孜自以建議幸蜀、收傳國寶、列聖真容、散家財犒軍爲己功，令宰相籓鎭共請加賞，上以令孜爲十軍兼十二衞觀軍容使。

translations.literal: Lingzi himself regarded as his merit advising the imperial progress to Shu, collecting transmitted national treasures, displaying ancestral portraits, and dispersing family wealth to reward the army; he had the chief ministers and military governors jointly request added rewards; the emperor made Lingzi commander observing the ten armies and twelve guards' military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Lingzi counted as his own achievements having urged the flight to Shu, securing the dynastic treasures and portraits of former emperors, and spending his private fortune to reward the troops. He had the chief ministers and regional governors petition jointly for further rewards, and the emperor appointed him military commissioner over the ten armies and twelve guard divisions.

sentences.zh: 成德節度使常山忠穆王王景崇死，軍中立其子節度副使鎔知留後事，時鎔生十年矣。

translations.literal: Chengde military commissioner Changshan Loyal and Solemn King Wang Jingchong died; the army established his son, deputy commissioner Rong, to know circuit affairs; at the time Rong was ten years old.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jingchong, military commissioner of Chengde and posthumously titled Loyal and Solemn King of Changshan, died. The army installed his ten-year-old son Rong, the deputy commissioner, as acting circuit administrator.

sentences.zh: 以天平留後朱瑄爲節度使。

translations.literal: Tianping acting commissioner Zhu Xuan was made military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xuan, acting administrator of Tianping, was appointed full military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 二月，壬子，李克用進軍乾干坑，與河中、易定、忠武軍合。

translations.literal: Second month, day renzi, Li Keyong advanced army to Qiangan Ravine, joining Hezhong, Yiding, and Zhongwu armies.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the day renzi, Li Keyong advanced to Qiangan Ravine and united with the forces of Hezhong, Yiding, and Zhongwu.

sentences.zh: 尚讓等將十五萬眾屯於梁田陂，明日，大戰，自午至晡，賊眾大敗，俘斬數萬，伏屍三十里。

translations.literal: Shang Rang and others led 150,000 masses encamped at Liangtian Slope; next day, great battle from noon to shen hour, rebel masses greatly defeated, captives and slain tens of thousands, corpses lying thirty li.
translations.idiomatic: Shang Rang and his commanders massed 150,000 men at Liangtian Slope. The next day they fought a great battle from noon until late afternoon. The rebel host was routed; tens of thousands were killed or captured, and the dead lay piled for thirty li.

sentences.zh: 巢將王璠、黃揆襲華州，據之，王遇亡去。

translations.literal: Chao's generals Wang Fan and Huang Kui raided Hua Prefecture, seized it; Wang Yu fled away.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Chao's generals Wang Fan and Huang Kui stormed Hua Prefecture and seized it; the defender Wang Yu fled.

sentences.zh: 初，光州刺史李罕之爲秦宗權所攻，棄州奔項城，帥餘眾歸諸葛爽，爽以爲懷州刺史。

translations.literal: Initially, Guang Prefecture governor Li Hanzhi was attacked by Qin Zongquan, abandoned the prefecture and fled to Xiangcheng, leading remaining masses to submit to Zhuge Shuang; Shuang made him Huaizhou governor.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Li Hanzhi, governor of Guang Prefecture, had been driven out by Qin Zongquan. He abandoned his post, fled to Xiangcheng, and led his surviving troops to Zhuge Shuang, who appointed him governor of Huaizhou.

sentences.zh: 韓簡攻鄆州，半年，不能下。

translations.literal: Han Jian attacked Yan Prefecture half a year, could not take it down.
translations.idiomatic: Han Jian besieged Yan Prefecture for six months without capturing it.

sentences.zh: 爽復襲取河陽，朱瑄請和，簡乃捨之，引兵襲河陽。

translations.literal: Shuang again raided and took Heyang; Zhu Xuan sought peace; Jian then released him and led troops to raid Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Shuang raided and recaptured Heyang. Zhu Xuan sued for peace, and Han Jian broke off the siege of Yan to march against Heyang instead.

sentences.zh: 爽遣罕之逆戰於武陟，魏軍大敗而還。

translations.literal: Shuang sent Hanzhi to meet in battle at Wuzhi; Wei army greatly defeated and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang sent Li Hanzhi to give battle at Wuzhi. The Wei army was routed and retreated.

sentences.zh: 大將澶州刺史樂行達先歸，據魏州，軍中共立行達爲留後，簡爲部下所殺。

translations.literal: Great general Duan Prefecture governor Yue Xingda returned first, seized Weizhou; the army together established Xingda as acting commissioner; Jian was killed by his subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: The great general Yue Xingda, governor of Duan Prefecture, returned ahead of the main force, seized Weizhou, and was proclaimed acting military commissioner by the troops. Han Jian was murdered by his own men.

sentences.zh: 己未，以行達爲魏博留後。

translations.literal: On the day jiwei, Xingda was made Weibo acting commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiwei, Yue Xingda was appointed acting commissioner of Weibo.

sentences.zh: 甲子，李克用進圍華州，黃思鄴、黃揆嬰城固守。

translations.literal: On the day jiazi, Li Keyong advanced to besiege Hua Prefecture; Huang Siye and Huang Kui relied on the city and firmly defended.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiazi, Li Keyong invested Hua Prefecture. Huang Siye and Huang Kui shut themselves within the walls and held firm.

sentences.zh: 克用分騎屯渭北。

translations.literal: Keyong divided cavalry to encamp north of the Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong detached cavalry to camp north of the Wei River.

sentences.zh: 以王鎔爲成德留後。

translations.literal: Wang Rong was made Chengde acting commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Rong was appointed acting military commissioner of Chengde.

sentences.zh: 以鄭紹業爲太子賓客、分司，以陳儒爲荊南留後。

translations.literal: Zheng Shaoye was made crown prince attendant and branch-office official; Chen Ru was made Jingnan acting commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Shaoye was appointed attendant to the crown prince with duties in the branch secretariat, and Chen Ru was made acting administrator of Jingnan.

sentences.zh: 峽路招討指揮使莊夢蝶韓秀升、屈行從所敗，退保忠州，應援使胡弘略戰亦不利。

translations.literal: Gorge-route campaign commander Zhuang Mengdie was defeated by Han Xiuyue and Qu Xingcong, retreated to defend Zhong Prefecture; relief envoy Hu Honglue's battle also was unfavorable.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuang Mengdie, the gorge-route pacification commander, was defeated by Han Xiuyue and Qu Xingcong and fell back to Zhong Prefecture. The relief commissioner Hu Honglue also fought without success.

sentences.zh: 江、淮貢賦皆爲賊所阻，百官無俸。

translations.literal: Yangtze and Huai tribute and taxes all were blocked by rebels; hundred officials had no salaries.
translations.idiomatic: Tribute from the Jianghuai region was cut off by the rebels, and the court officials went unpaid.

sentences.zh: 雲安、淯井路不通，民間乏鹽。

translations.literal: Yun'an and Yujing routes were not passable; among the people salt was lacking.
translations.idiomatic: The routes through Yun'an and Yujing were blocked, and salt grew scarce among the populace.

sentences.zh: 陳敬瑄奏以眉州防禦使高仁厚爲西川行軍司馬，將三千兵討之。

translations.literal: Chen Jingxuan memorialized making Meizhou defense commissioner Gao Renhou western Sichuan campaign deputy commander, leading three thousand troops to campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jingxuan recommended Gao Renhou, defense commissioner of Meizhou, as deputy commander of the western Sichuan expedition, to lead three thousand men against the rebels.

sentences.zh: 加鳳翔節度使李昌言同平章事。

translations.literal: Fengxiang military commissioner Li Changyan was added as co-chief councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Li Changyan, military commissioner of Fengxiang, was appointed an associate chief councilor.

sentences.zh: 黃巢兵數敗，食復盡，陰爲遁計，發兵三萬扼藍田道。

translations.literal: Huang Chao's army repeatedly defeated, food again exhausted, secretly made escape plans, sent army thirty thousand to block Lantian road.
