translations.idiomatic: Huang Chao's forces had suffered repeated defeats and again ran out of provisions. He secretly planned retreat and dispatched thirty thousand men to hold the Lantian road.

sentences.zh: 三月，壬申，遣尚讓將兵救華州。

translations.literal: Third month, day renshen, sent Shang Rang to lead troops to rescue Hua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on the day renshen, he sent Shang Rang with an army to relieve Hua Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 李克用、王重榮引兵逆戰於零口，破之。

translations.literal: Li Keyong and Wang Chongrong led troops to meet in battle at Lingkou, broke them.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong and Wang Chongrong met the relief force at Lingkou and shattered it.

sentences.zh: 克用進軍渭橋，騎軍在渭北，克用每夜令其將薛志勤、康君立潛入長安，燔積聚，斬虜而還，賊中大驚。

translations.literal: Keyong advanced army to Wei Bridge, cavalry army north of Wei; each night Keyong ordered his generals Xue Zhiqin and Kang Junli secretly to enter Chang'an, burn stores, behead captives and return; among rebels great alarm.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong pressed toward Wei Bridge with his cavalry on the north bank. Each night he sent his generals Xue Zhiqin and Kang Junli into Chang'an to burn supplies, kill stragglers, and withdraw before dawn. Panic spread through the rebel ranks.

sentences.zh: 以淮南押牙合肥楊行愍爲廬州刺史。

translations.literal: Huainan guard officer Hefei Yang Xingmin was made Luzhou governor.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xingmin of Hefei, a guard officer under the Huainan command, was appointed governor of Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 行愍本廬州牙將，勇敢，屢有戰功，都將忌之，白刺史郎幼復遣使出戍於外。

translations.literal: Xingmin was originally Luzhou guard general, brave, repeatedly had battle achievements; the chief general envied him, informed the governor Lang Yourfu to send him out on external garrison duty.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xingmin had been a guard officer in Luzhou, bold and repeatedly distinguished in battle. The chief commander grew jealous and persuaded Governor Lang Yourfu to post him on distant border duty.

sentences.zh: 行愍過辭，都將以甘言悅之，問其所須，行愍曰：「正須汝頭耳！」

translations.literal: Xingmin passed to take leave; the chief general with sweet words pleased him, asked what he needed; Xingmin said: "Just need your head!"
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Xingmin came to bid farewell, the chief commander flattered him and asked what he might need. Yang Xingmin replied, "Nothing but your head!"

sentences.zh: 遂起斬之，並將諸營，自稱八營都知兵馬使。

translations.literal: Then he rose and beheaded him, also led all camps, styled himself eight-camps overall knowing army and horse commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He sprang up and slew him on the spot, took command of every camp, and styled himself overall commander of the eight garrisons.

sentences.zh: 幼復不能制，薦於高駢，請以自代。

translations.literal: Yourfu could not control him, recommended him to Gao Pian, requested to be replaced by him.
translations.idiomatic: Lang Yourfu could not restrain him and therefore recommended him to Gao Pian, asking to resign in Yang's favor.

sentences.zh: 駢以行愍爲淮南押牙，知廬州事，朝廷因而命之。

translations.literal: Pian made Xingmin Huainan guard officer, knowing Luzhou affairs; the court accordingly appointed him.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Pian named him his guard officer and governor of Luzhou, and the court confirmed the appointment.

sentences.zh: 行愍聞州人王勖賢，召，欲用之，固徉。

translations.literal: Xingmin heard Luzhou man Wang Jin was worthy, summoned him, wished to employ him; he firmly feigned illness.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that Wang Jin, a man of Luzhou, had a fine reputation, Yang summoned him for service, but Wang stubbornly feigned illness.

sentences.zh: 問其子弟，曰：「子潛，好學慎密，可任以事；

translations.literal: Asked his sons and younger brothers, said: "Son Qian, loves learning and is careful and close, can be entrusted with affairs;
translations.idiomatic: Yang asked Jin's household instead. They said, "His son Qian is studious and discreet and can be trusted with affairs;

sentences.zh: 弟子稔，有氣節，可爲將。」

translations.literal: younger brother's son Ren, has spirit and integrity, can be a general."
translations.idiomatic: his nephew Ren has spirit and can serve as a commander."

sentences.zh: 行愍召潛置門下，以稔及定遠人季章爲騎將。

translations.literal: Xingmin summoned Qian and placed him under his gate, made Ren and Dingyuan man Ji Zhang cavalry generals.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xingmin took Qian into his staff and appointed Ren and Ji Zhang of Dingyuan as cavalry commanders.

sentences.zh: 初，呂用之因左驍雄軍使俞公楚得見高駢。

translations.literal: Initially, Lü Yongzhi through Left Valiant Eagle army commissioner Yu Gongchu obtained audience with Gao Pian.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Yongzhi had first gained access to Gao Pian through Yu Gongchu, commander of the Left Valiant Eagle Army.

sentences.zh: 用之橫甚，或以咎公楚，公楚數戒用之少自斂，毋相累，用之銜之。

translations.literal: Yongzhi was very overbearing; some blamed Gongchu; Gongchu repeatedly admonished Yongzhi to restrain himself somewhat, not implicate each other; Yongzhi harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhi grew ever more arrogant, and blame fell on Yu Gongchu, who repeatedly warned him to restrain himself lest they both be ruined. Yongzhi bore a grudge.

sentences.zh: 右驍雄軍使姚歸禮氣直敢言，尤疾用之所爲，時面數其罪，常欲手刃之。

translations.literal: Right Valiant Eagle army commissioner Yao Guili was straight in spirit and dared speak, especially hated Yongzhi's conduct, often faced him counting his crimes, often wished to cut him down with his own hand.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Guili, commander of the Right Valiant Eagle Army, was blunt and fearless. He detested Yongzhi's conduct, often denounced him to his face, and longed to kill him with his own blade.

sentences.zh: 癸未夜，用之與其黨會倡家，歸禮潛遣人爇其室，殺貌類者數人，用之易服得免。

translations.literal: On the night of guiwei, Yongzhi and his faction met at a singing-house; Guili secretly sent men to burn his room, killed several who resembled him in appearance; Yongzhi changed clothes and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of guiwei, Yongzhi and his clique were at a brothel when Guili secretly set fire to the building. Several men who resembled Yongzhi were killed in the blaze, but Yongzhi swapped clothes and escaped.

sentences.zh: 明旦，窮治其事，獲縱火者，皆驍雄之卒。

translations.literal: Next dawn, thoroughly investigated the affair, seized the fire-setters; all were Valiant Eagle troops.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the authorities traced the arson and seized the culprits, all soldiers of the Valiant Eagle armies.

sentences.zh: 用之於是日夜譖二將於駢。

translations.literal: Yongzhi from this night and day slandered the two generals to Pian.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhi then began night and day to slander the two commanders to Gao Pian.

sentences.zh: 未幾，駢使二將將驍雄卒三千襲賊於慎縣，用之密以語楊行愍云：「公楚、歸禮欲襲廬州。」

translations.literal: Before long, Pian ordered the two generals to lead Valiant Eagle troops three thousand to raid rebels at Shen County; Yongzhi secretly told Yang Xingmin saying: "Gongchu and Guili wish to raid Luzhou."
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Gao Pian ordered the two commanders to lead three thousand Valiant Eagle troops on a raid into Shen County. Yongzhi secretly told Yang Xingmin that Gongchu and Guili were plotting to attack Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 行愍發兵掩之，二將不爲備，舉軍盡殪，以二將謀亂告駢。

translations.literal: Xingmin sent troops to ambush them; the two generals were unprepared; the whole army was annihilated; he reported to Pian that the two generals plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xingmin sent troops in ambush. The two commanders were taken unawares and their entire force was wiped out. Yang reported to Gao Pian that they had plotted rebellion.

sentences.zh: 駢不知用之謀，厚賞行愍。

translations.literal: Pian did not know Yongzhi's plot, richly rewarded Xingmin.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Pian, unaware of Yongzhi's scheme, richly rewarded Yang Xingmin.

sentences.zh: 己丑，以河中行營招討副使朱全忠爲宣武節度使，俟克復長安，令赴鎭。

translations.literal: On the day jichou, Hezhong campaign army deputy punitive envoy Zhu Quanzhong was made Xuanwu military commissioner; when Chang'an was recovered he was ordered to go to his post.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jichou, Zhu Quanzhong, deputy campaign commander in Hezhong, was appointed military commissioner of Xuanwu, with orders to take up the post once Chang'an was recovered.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，李克用等拔華州，黃揆棄城走。

translations.literal: On the day guisi, Li Keyong and others took Hua Prefecture; Huang Kui abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: On the day guisi, Li Keyong and his allies captured Hua Prefecture, and Huang Kui abandoned the city and fled.

sentences.zh: 劉漢宏分兵屯黃嶺、巖下、貞女三鎭，錢鏐將八都兵自富春擊之，破黃嶺，擒巖下鎭將史弁、貞女鎭將楊元宗。

translations.literal: Liu Hanhong divided troops to garrison Huangling, Yanxia, and Zhennü three posts; Qian Liu led Eight-Districts army from Fuchun to attack them, broke Huangling, captured Yanxia post commander Shi Bian and Zhennü post commander Yang Yuanzong.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hanhong stationed detachments at the posts of Huangling, Yanxia, and Zhennü. Qian Liu led his Eight-Districts army from Fuchun, routed the force at Huangling, and captured Shi Bian at Yanxia and Yang Yuanzong at Zhennü.

sentences.zh: 漢安以精兵屯諸暨，鏐又擊破之，漢宏走。

translations.literal: Han'an with elite troops encamped at Zhuji; Liu again attacked and broke them; Hanhong fled.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hanhong concentrated elite troops at Zhuji, but Qian Liu defeated them there as well and Hanhong fled.

sentences.zh: 莊夢蝶與韓秀升、屈行從戰，又敗。

translations.literal: Zhuang Mengdie fought with Han Xiuyue and Qu Xingcong, was again defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuang Mengdie met Han Xiuyue and Qu Xingcong in battle and was defeated again.

sentences.zh: 其敗兵紛紜還走，所在慰諭，不可遏。

translations.literal: His defeated troops in confusion returned fleeing; wherever they were comforted and instructed, they could not be stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The routed troops stampeded homeward and could not be halted, no matter who tried to calm them.

sentences.zh: 遇高仁厚於路，叱之，即止。

translations.literal: They met Gao Renhou on the road; he shouted at them, and they stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Renhou met them on the road, shouted them down, and they halted at once.

sentences.zh: 仁厚斬都虞候一人，更令修娖部伍。

translations.literal: Renhou beheaded one army overseer, again ordered to repair and discipline the troops.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Renhou executed one army overseer, reorganized the ranks, and restored discipline.

sentences.zh: 乃召耆老，詢以山川蹊徑及賊寨所據，喜曰：「賊精兵盡在舟中，使老弱守寨，資糧皆在寨中，此所謂重戰輕防，其敗必矣！」

translations.literal: Then he summoned elders, inquired about mountain paths and where rebel camps were held, rejoiced and said: "Rebels' elite troops all are in boats, making old and weak guard camps, provisions all in camps; this is what is called heavy in battle and light in defense; their defeat is certain!"
translations.idiomatic: He questioned local elders about mountain paths and rebel positions and exclaimed with satisfaction, "The rebels keep their best troops afloat while the old and weak guard the camps, and all their supplies are stored ashore. They are fighting hard while neglecting defense. They are bound to fall!"

sentences.zh: 乃揚兵江上，爲欲涉之狀。

translations.literal: Then he displayed troops on the river, as if wishing to cross.
translations.idiomatic: He then paraded his troops along the river as though preparing to ford it.

sentences.zh: 賊晝夜御備，遣兵挑戰，仁厚不與交兵，潛發勇士千人執兵負稿，夜，由間道攻其寨，且焚之。

translations.literal: Rebels day and night prepared defense, sent troops to provoke battle; Renhou did not join battle, secretly sent brave warriors a thousand bearing arms and carrying straw, at night by secret path attacked their camp and also burned it.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels stood guard day and night and sent parties to provoke a fight, but Renhou refused battle. By night he secretly led a thousand picked men with arms and bundles of straw along a hidden path to storm and burn their camp.

sentences.zh: 賊望見，分兵往救之不及，資糧蕩盡，眾心已搖。

translations.literal: Rebels saw from afar, divided troops to rescue but could not arrive in time; provisions were swept away, the masses' hearts already shaken.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels saw the flames and sent detachments to save the camp, but too late; their stores were destroyed and morale collapsed.

sentences.zh: 仁厚復募善游者鑿其舟底，相繼皆沉，賊往來惶惑，不能相救，仁厚遣兵於要路邀擊，且招之，賊眾皆降。

translations.literal: Renhou again recruited skilled swimmers to bore the bottoms of their boats; one after another all sank; rebels going back and forth panicked and confused, could not rescue each other; Renhou sent troops at key roads to intercept and also to summon them; rebel masses all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Renhou hired divers to bore holes in the rebel boats until they sank one after another. Stranded rebels panicked and could not aid one another. His men blocked the crossings, offered terms, and the rebel host surrendered.

sentences.zh: 秀升、行從見眾潰，揮劍亂斫，欲止之。

translations.literal: Xiuyue and Xingcong saw the masses routed, waved swords hacking wildly, wished to stop them.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Xiuyue and Qu Xingcong saw the rout, they flailed their swords wildly, trying to stem the flight.

sentences.zh: 眾愈怒，共執二人詣仁厚，仁厚詰之曰：「何故反？」

translations.literal: The masses grew angrier, together seized the two men and brought them to Renhou; Renhou interrogated them saying: "Why do you rebel?"
translations.idiomatic: The men only grew more furious, seized both leaders, and hauled them before Gao Renhou, who demanded, "Why have you rebelled?"

sentences.zh: 秀長曰：「自大中皇帝晏駕，天下無復公道，紐解綱絶。

translations.literal: Xiuchang said: "Since Great Zhong emperor passed away, under heaven there is no longer fairness; buttons undone, net broken.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuchang answered, "Since Emperor Da Zhong died, justice has vanished from the realm. Laws and bonds alike have snapped.

sentences.zh: 今日反者，豈惟秀升！

translations.literal: Today those who rebel, how are they only Xiuyue!
translations.idiomatic: Rebels today are hardly limited to Xiuyue and me!

sentences.zh: 成是敗非，機上之肉，惟所烹醢耳！」

translations.literal: Success is wrong, defeat is not; meat on the chopping block, only as one cooks and minces.
translations.idiomatic: Success or failure is not the point. We are meat on the block, to be stewed or minced as you please!

sentences.zh: 仁厚愀然，命善食而械之。

translations.literal: Renhou looked grim, ordered good food and shackled them.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Renhou's face darkened, but he gave them a good meal before putting them in fetters.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，庚子，獻於行在，斬之。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, day gengzi, presented at the mobile court, beheaded them.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on the day gengzi, they were sent to the emperor's camp and executed.

sentences.zh: 李克用與忠武將龐從、河中將白志遷等引兵先進，與黃巢軍戰於渭南，一日三戰，皆捷。

translations.literal: Li Keyong with Zhongwu general Pang Cong, Hezhong general Bai Zhilian and others led troops forward first, with Huang Chao's army battled at Weinan; in one day three battles, all victorious.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong advanced with Pang Cong of Zhongwu and Bai Zhilian of Hezhong and fought Huang Chao's army at Weinan three times in a single day, winning each engagement.

sentences.zh: 義成、義武等諸軍繼之，賊眾大奔。

translations.literal: Yicheng, Yiwu and other armies followed; rebel masses greatly fled.
translations.idiomatic: The armies of Yicheng, Yiwu, and other circuits pressed behind them, and the rebel host broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，克用等自光泰門入京師，黃巢力戰不勝，焚宮室遁去。

translations.literal: On the day jiachen, Keyong and others from Guangtai Gate entered the capital; Huang Chao fought hard but could not win, burned palace halls and fled away.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiachen, Li Keyong and his allies entered the capital through Guangtai Gate. Huang Chao fought fiercely, failed to hold, set the palaces ablaze, and fled.

sentences.zh: 賊死及降者甚眾，官軍暴掠，無異於賊，長安室屋及民所存無幾。

translations.literal: Rebels dead and surrendered were very many; government armies violently plundered, no different from rebels; Chang'an houses and what civilians had left were few.
translations.idiomatic: Vast numbers of rebels were killed or surrendered, but the imperial armies looted as savagely as the rebels had, and little of Chang'an's buildings or civilian property survived.

sentences.zh: 巢自藍田入商山，多遺珍寶於路。

translations.literal: Chao from Lantian entered Shang Mountains, left many treasures on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Chao withdrew from Lantian into the Shang Mountains, strewing treasures along the road.

sentences.zh: 官軍爭取之，不急追，賊遂逸去。

translations.literal: Government armies scrambled to take them, did not urgently pursue; rebels thus escaped away.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers stopped to seize the booty instead of pressing the pursuit, and the rebels escaped.

sentences.zh: 楊復光遣使告捷，百官入賀。

translations.literal: Yang Fuguang sent envoy to report victory; hundred officials entered to congratulate.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fuguang sent envoys with news of victory, and the officials offered congratulations.

sentences.zh: 詔留忠武等軍二萬人，委大明宮留守王徽及京畿制置使田從異部分，守衞長安。

translations.literal: Edict left Zhongwu and other armies twenty thousand men, entrusted to Daming Palace defender Wang Hui and capital-region disposition commissioner Tian Congyi to divide and assign, to guard and defend Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: An edict left twenty thousand men from Zhongwu and allied armies, under the Daming Palace defender Wang Hui and the capital disposition commissioner Tian Congyi, to garrison Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 五月，加朱玫、李克用、東方逵同平章事。

translations.literal: Fifth month, Zhu Mei, Li Keyong, and Dongfang Kui were added as co-chief councilors.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, Zhu Mei, Li Keyong, and Dongfang Kui were made associate chief councilors.

sentences.zh: 升陝州爲節度使，以王重盈爲節度。

translations.literal: Shaan Prefecture was promoted to military commission; Wang Chongying was made military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Shaan Prefecture was elevated to a full military commission, with Wang Chongying as its commissioner.

sentences.zh: 又建延州爲保塞軍，以保大行軍司馬、延州刺史李孝恭爲節度使。

translations.literal: Again Yan Prefecture was established as Baosai Army; Baoda campaign deputy commander, Yan governor Li Xiaogong was made military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Prefecture was made the Baosai circuit, and Li Xiaogong, deputy commander of the Baoda expedition and governor of Yan, was appointed its military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 克用時年二十八，於諸將最少，而破黃巢，復長安，功第一，兵勢最強，諸將皆畏之。

translations.literal: Keyong at the time was twenty-eight years old, among all generals the youngest, yet broke Huang Chao, recovered Chang'an, merit first, military power strongest, all generals feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong was only twenty-eight, the youngest of the major commanders, yet he had broken Huang Chao and recovered Chang'an. His merit ranked first and his army was the strongest; the other generals all feared him.

sentences.zh: 克用一目微眇，時人謂之「獨眼龍」。

translations.literal: Keyong had one eye slightly blind; people of the time called him "One-Eyed Dragon."
translations.idiomatic: One of Li Keyong's eyes was dim, and men called him the One-Eyed Dragon.

sentences.zh: 詔以崔璆家貴身顯，爲黃巢相首尾三載，不逃不隱，於所在斬之。

translations.literal: Edict because Cui Yan was from a noble house and body eminent, for Huang Chao from beginning to end three years neither fled nor hid, at wherever he was beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the execution of Cui Yan wherever found. Born to a prominent family and himself a high official, he had served Huang Chao openly for three years without fleeing or concealing his allegiance.

sentences.zh: 黃巢使其驍將孟楷將萬人爲前鋒，擊蔡州，節度使秦宗權逆戰而敗。

translations.literal: Huang Chao ordered his fierce general Meng Kai to lead ten thousand as vanguard, attack Cai Prefecture; military commissioner Qin Zongquan met battle and was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Chao sent his fierce general Meng Kai ahead with ten thousand men against Cai Prefecture. Military Commissioner Qin Zongquan met him in battle and was defeated.

sentences.zh: 賊進攻其城，宗權遂稱臣於巢，與之連兵。

translations.literal: Rebels advanced to attack his city; Zongquan then declared himself subject to Chao, linked armies with him.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels pressed the siege. Zongquan then submitted to Huang Chao and joined forces with him.

sentences.zh: 初，巢在長安，陳州刺史宛丘趙犨謂將佐曰：「巢不死長安，必東走，陳其沖也。

translations.literal: Initially, when Chao was in Chang'an, Chen Prefecture governor Wancheng Zhao Chou told staff officers: "If Chao does not die in Chang'an, he must flee east; Chen is his thoroughfare.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while Huang Chao still held Chang'an, Zhao Chou of Wancheng, governor of Chen Prefecture, told his officers, "If Chao does not die in the capital, he will march east, and Chen lies on his road.

sentences.zh: 且巢素與忠武爲仇，不可不爲之備。」

translations.literal: Moreover Chao from of old was enemy with Zhongwu; cannot fail to prepare for it."
translations.idiomatic: He has long been at feud with Zhongwu. We must prepare."

sentences.zh: 乃完城塹，繕甲兵，積芻粟；

translations.literal: Then he completed walls and moats, repaired armor and weapons, stored fodder and grain;
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Chou repaired the walls and moats, readied arms and armor, and stockpiled fodder and grain;

sentences.zh: 六十里之內，民有資糧者，悉徙之入城。

translations.literal: Within sixty li, people who had provisions were all moved into the city.
translations.idiomatic: Every household with food within sixty li was moved inside the walls.

sentences.zh: 多募勇士，使其弟昶珝、子麓林分將之。

translations.literal: He widely recruited brave warriors, had his younger brothers Chang Xu and son Lu Lin divide command of them.
translations.idiomatic: He recruited brave men widely and put his brothers Chang and Xu and his son Lu Lin in separate commands.

sentences.zh: 孟楷既下蔡州，移兵擊陳，軍於項城。

translations.literal: Meng Kai having taken Cai Prefecture, moved troops to attack Chen, encamped army at Xiangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: After Meng Kai took Cai Prefecture, he shifted against Chen and encamped at Xiangcheng.

sentences.zh: 犨先示之弱，伺其無備，襲擊之，殺獲殆盡，生擒楷，斬之。

translations.literal: Chou first showed them weakness, waited until they were unprepared, raided and attacked them, killed and captured nearly all, seized Kai alive, beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Chou feigned weakness, then struck when the enemy was off guard. He nearly annihilated the force, took Meng Kai alive, and executed him.

sentences.zh: 巢聞楷死，驚怒，悉眾屯殷水。

translations.literal: Chao heard Kai dead, startled and angry, brought all masses to encamp at Yinshui.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Chao, shocked and enraged at Kai's death, marched his entire host to Yinshui.

sentences.zh: 六月，與秦宗權合兵圍陳州，掘塹五重，百道攻之。

translations.literal: Sixth month, with Qin Zongquan united armies to besiege Chen Prefecture, dug moats five layers, attacked from a hundred routes.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he and Qin Zongquan united to besiege Chen, digging five rings of trenches and assaulting from a hundred directions.

sentences.zh: 陳人大恐，犨諭之曰：「忠武素著義勇，陳州號爲勁兵，況吾家久食陳祿，誓與此州存亡。

translations.literal: Chen people greatly feared; Chou instructed them saying: "Zhongwu from of old is known for righteous courage; Chen Prefecture is called tough troops; moreover our house long ate Chen salaries, swear with this prefecture to live or die together.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Chen were terrified. Zhao Chou rallied them: "Zhongwu has always been famed for valor, and Chenzhou troops are counted among the empire's best. My family has long lived on Chen's pay. I swear to live and die with this city.

sentences.zh: 男子當求生於死中，且徇國而死，不愈於臣賊而生乎！

translations.literal: Men ought to seek life within death; moreover to die for the state, is it not better than to serve rebels and live!
translations.idiomatic: A man should seek life in the jaws of death. To die for the dynasty is better than to bow to rebels and live!

sentences.zh: 有異議者斬！」

translations.literal: Whoever has different opinion, behead!
translations.idiomatic: Whoever disagrees will be beheaded!

sentences.zh: 數引銳兵開門出擊賊。

translations.literal: Repeatedly led elite troops opening gates to sally out and attack rebels.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly led crack troops out the gates to strike the besiegers.

sentences.zh: 破之。

translations.literal: Broke them.
translations.idiomatic: And drove them back each time.

sentences.zh: 巢益怒，營於州北，立宮室百司，爲持久之計。

translations.literal: Chao grew angrier, encamped north of the prefecture, erected palace halls and hundred offices, made long-term plans.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Chao, furious, pitched camp north of the city, raised palaces and government halls, and settled in for a long siege.

sentences.zh: 時民間無積聚，賊掠人爲糧，生投於碓磑，並骨食之，號給糧之處曰「舂磨寨」。

translations.literal: At the time among the people there were no stores; rebels plundered people for grain, threw them alive into mortars and millstones, together with bones ate them, called the place supplying grain "Pounding-and-grinding Stockade."
translations.idiomatic: With no grain left in the countryside, the rebels seized people for food, threw the living into pestles and millstones, and ate flesh and bone together. They named the supply camps the Pounding-and-Grinding Stockades.

sentences.zh: 縱兵四掠，自河南、許、汝、唐、鄧、孟、鄭、汴、曹、濮、徐、兗等數十州，鹹被其毒。

translations.literal: They released troops to plunder in four directions, from Henan, Xu, Ru, Tang, Deng, Meng, Zheng, Bian, Cao, Pu, Xu, Yan and other several tens of prefectures, all suffered their poison.
translations.idiomatic: They sent their soldiers to ravage the countryside throughout dozens of prefectures from Henan, Xu, Ru, Tang, Deng, Meng, Zheng, Bian, Cao, Pu, Xu, Yan, and beyond, until the region was utterly scourged.

sentences.zh: 初，上蔡人劉謙爲嶺南小校，節度使韋宙奇其器，以兄女妻之。

translations.literal: Initially, Liu Qian of Shangcai was a junior officer in Lingnan; Military Commissioner Wei Zhou marveled at his talent and gave him his elder brother's daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Liu Qian of Shangcai had served as a junior officer in Lingnan. Military Commissioner Wei Zhou was struck by his ability and married him to his elder brother's daughter.

sentences.zh: 謙擊群盜，屢有功，辛丑，以謙爲封州刺史。

translations.literal: Qian attacked bandit gangs and won repeated success; on the day xinchou he was appointed prefect of Feng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Qian raided outlaw bands with repeated success, and on the day xinchou he was appointed prefect of Feng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 加東川節度使楊師立同平章事。

translations.literal: Dongchuan Military Commissioner Yang Shili was added as co-chief councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Shili, military commissioner of Dongchuan, was made associate chief councilor.

sentences.zh: 宣武節度使朱全忠帥所部數百人赴鎭，秋，七月，丁卯，至汴州。

translations.literal: Xuanwu Military Commissioner Zhu Quanzhong led several hundred of his men to take up his commission; in autumn, the seventh month, on the day dingmao, he reached Bian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong, military commissioner of Xuanwu, marched several hundred of his men to take up his commission. In autumn, the seventh month, on the day dingmao, he reached Bian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時汴、宋荐饑，公私窮竭，內外驕軍難制，外爲大敵所攻，無日不戰，眾心危懼，而全忠勇氣益振。

translations.literal: At the time Bian and Song suffered famine after famine; public and private resources were exhausted; the arrogant garrisons within and without were hard to control; outwardly they were attacked by a great enemy, and not a day passed without battle; popular hearts were fearful, yet Quanzhong's courage grew all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Bian and Song were gripped by famine after famine. Public and private resources were spent, the arrogant garrisons within and without were barely controllable, and a powerful foe pressed the borders with fighting every day. Morale was fraying, yet Zhu Quanzhong's fighting spirit only grew.

sentences.zh: 詔以黃巢未平，加全忠東北面都招討使。

translations.literal: An edict: because Huang Chao was not yet pacified, Quanzhong was added as grand punitive commissioner of the northeast.
translations.idiomatic: Because Huang Chao was not yet subdued, an edict made Zhu Quanzhong grand punitive commissioner of the northeast.

sentences.zh: 南詔遣布燮楊奇肱來迎公主。

translations.literal: Nanzhao sent the bufie Yang Qigong to come welcome the princess.
translations.idiomatic: Nanzhao dispatched the bufie Yang Qigong to escort the princess.

sentences.zh: 詔陳敬瑄與書，辭以「鑾輿巡幸，儀物未備，俟還京邑，然後出降。」

translations.literal: An edict ordered Chen Jingxuan to write a letter, declining on the grounds that "the imperial carriage is on tour, ceremonial objects are not yet prepared; wait until we return to the capital, then we will send her out for marriage."
translations.idiomatic: The court told Chen Jingxuan to reply in writing, pleading that "the emperor is still on campaign, the wedding equipage is not ready, and the princess will be sent only after we return to the capital."

sentences.zh: 奇肱不從，直前至成都。

translations.literal: Qigong did not comply and pressed straight on to Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Qigong refused to accept this and pressed on to Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 李克用自長安引兵還雁門，尋有詔，以克用爲河東節度使，召鄭從讜詣行在。

translations.literal: Li Keyong led troops back from Chang'an toward Yanmen; soon there was an edict making Keyong Hedong military commissioner and summoning Zheng Congdian to the mobile court.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong withdrew from Chang'an toward Yanmen. Soon an edict appointed him military commissioner of Hedong and summoned Zheng Congdian to the emperor's camp.

sentences.zh: 克用乃自東道過榆次，詣雁門省其父。

translations.literal: Keyong then by the eastern route passed Yuci and went to Yanmen to visit his father.
translations.idiomatic: He took the eastern road through Yuci to Yanmen to see his father.

sentences.zh: 克用尋榜河東，安慰軍民曰：「勿爲舊念，各安家業。」

translations.literal: Keyong soon posted proclamation in Hedong, comforting army and people, saying: "Do not hold to old grudges; each settle in your homes and livelihoods."
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he posted notices across Hedong reassuring soldiers and civilians: "Let go of old grievances and return to your homes and trades."

sentences.zh: 左驍衞上將軍楊復光卒於河中。

translations.literal: Left Brave Guards senior general Yang Fuguang died at Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fuguang, senior general of the Left Brave Guards, died at Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 復光慷慨喜忠義，善撫士卒，軍中慟哭累日，八都將鹿晏弘等各以其眾散去。

translations.literal: Fuguang was magnanimous and loved loyalty and righteousness; he was good at comforting soldiers; in the army they mourned and wept for many days; Eight-Districts generals such as Lu Yanhong each led their masses away and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fuguang was open-handed and devoted to loyalty; he knew how to win over his troops. The army mourned him for days. Generals of the Eight Districts, including Lu Yanhong, each led their men away in separate bands.

sentences.zh: 田令孜素畏忌之，聞其卒，甚喜，因擯斥其兄樞密使復恭爲飛龍使。

translations.literal: Tian Lingzi had long feared and envied him; hearing of his death, he greatly rejoiced; therefore he expelled his elder brother Privy Councilor Fugong, demoting him to Feilong commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Lingzi had long feared and resented him. On hearing of his death he was delighted and removed Yang Fuguang's elder brother, Privy Councilor Yang Fugong, demoting him to commissioner of the Feilong Bureau.

sentences.zh: 令孜專權，人莫與之抗，惟復恭數與之爭得失，故令孜惡之，復恭因稱疾歸藍田。

translations.literal: Lingzi monopolized power; no one matched him in resistance; only Fugong repeatedly with him argued gains and losses; therefore Lingzi hated him; Fugong thus claimed illness and returned to Lantian.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Lingzi held unchecked power and few dared oppose him. Yang Fugong alone argued with him repeatedly over policy, which earned Tian's hatred. Fugong feigned illness and retired to Lantian.

sentences.zh: 以成德留後王鎔、魏博留後樂行達、天平留後朱瑄爲本道節度使。

translations.literal: Chengde regent Wang Rong, Weibo regent Yue Xingda, and Tianping regent Zhu Xuan were made military commissioners of their respective circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Rong of Chengde, Yue Xingda of Weibo, and Zhu Xuan of Tianping were confirmed as full military commissioners of their circuits.

sentences.zh: 司徒、門下侍郎、同平章事鄭畋，雖當播越，猶謹法度。

translations.literal: Situ, Gate Department vice-director, co-chief councilor Zheng Tian, although amid displacement, still observed law and regulation strictly.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Tian, grand tutor, vice-director of the Gate Department, and associate chief councilor, kept to proper procedure even in the turmoil of exile.

sentences.zh: 田令孜爲判官呉圓求郎官，畋不許；

translations.literal: Tian Lingzi for his aide Wu Yuan sought a court gentleman post; Tian did not permit;
translations.idiomatic: Tian Lingzi asked him to grant a court office to his aide Wu Yuan; Zheng Tian refused.

sentences.zh: 陳敬瑄欲立於宰相之上，畋以故事，使相品秩雖高，皆居真相之下，固爭之；

translations.literal: Chen Jingxuan wished to stand above chief councilors; Tian by precedent held that military commissioners, though high in rank, all stood below true chancellors, and firmly contended;
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jingxuan wanted precedence over the civil chancellors. Zheng Tian cited precedent: however exalted a military commissioner might be, he remained below the true chancellor—and held his ground.

sentences.zh: 二人乃令鳳翔節度使李昌言上言：「軍情猜忌，不可令畋扈從過此。」

translations.literal: The two men then ordered Fengxiang Military Commissioner Li Changyan to memorialize: "Army sentiments are suspicious and wary; Tian must not be allowed to accompany past here."
translations.idiomatic: The two men had Li Changyan, military commissioner of Fengxiang, memorialize that "the troops are suspicious and uneasy; Zheng Tian must not be allowed to accompany the court beyond this point."

sentences.zh: 畋亦累表辭位，乃罷爲太子太保，又以其子兵部侍郎凝績爲彭州刺史，使之就養。

translations.literal: Tian also repeatedly submitted memorials resigning his post; he was then dismissed as Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, and his son Ministry of War vice-director Ningji was made Pengzhou prefect so that he might go to support his father's care.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Tian too submitted repeated resignations and was removed to Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent. His son Ningji, vice-director of the Ministry of War, was appointed prefect of Pengzhou so he could tend his father.

sentences.zh: 以兵部尚書判度支裴澈爲中書侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: Ministry of War director concurrently managing finance Pei Che was made Secretariat vice-director, co-chief councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Che, director of the Ministry of War acting as finance chief, was made Secretariat vice-director and associate chief councilor.

sentences.zh: 八月，甲辰，李克用至晉陽，詔以前振武節度使李國昌爲代北節度使，鎭代州。

translations.literal: Eighth month, day jiachen, Li Keyong reached Jinyang; an edict made former Zhenwu Military Commissioner Li Guochang Daibei military commissioner, garrisoning Daizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on the day jiachen, Li Keyong reached Jinyang. An edict appointed his father Li Guochang, former commissioner of Zhenwu, military commissioner of Daibei with his seat at Daizhou.

sentences.zh: 升湖南爲欽化軍，以觀察使閔勖爲節度使。

translations.literal: Hunan was promoted to Qinhua Army; observation commissioner Min Xu was made military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Hunan was elevated to the Qinhua circuit, and Min Xu, the observation commissioner, was made its military governor.

sentences.zh: 九月，如陳敬瑄兼中書令，進爵穎川郡王。

translations.literal: Ninth month, Chen Jingxuan was additionally made Zhongshu Ling and advanced in rank to Prince of Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Chen Jingxuan was also made director of the Secretariat and raised to Prince of Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 感化節度使時溥營於殷水；

translations.literal: Ganhua Military Commissioner Shi Pu encamped at Yinshui;
translations.idiomatic: Shi Pu, military commissioner of Ganhua, encamped at Yinshui;

sentences.zh: 加溥東面兵馬都統。

translations.literal: Pu was added as grand marshal of eastern armies and horses.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Pu was made grand marshal of eastern armies.

sentences.zh: 以荊南留後陳儒爲節度使。

translations.literal: Jingnan regent Chen Ru was made military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Ru, regent of Jingnan, was confirmed as military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 昭義節度使孟方立，以潞州地險人勁，屢篡主帥，欲漸弱之，及遷治所於邢州，大將家及富室皆徙山東，潞人不悅。

translations.literal: Zhaoyi Military Commissioner Meng Fangli, because Luzhou's land was dangerous and its people fierce, with commanders repeatedly usurped, wished gradually to weaken it; when he moved his seat of government to Xingzhou, great generals' families and wealthy houses were all moved to Shandong; Luzhou people were displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Fangli of Zhaoyi found Luzhou's terrain formidable and its people warlike, with commanders often overthrown. To weaken the prefecture he moved his headquarters to Xingzhou and relocated leading families and the wealthy east of the Taihang Mountains. The people of Luzhou were bitterly resentful.

sentences.zh: 監軍祁審誨因人心不安，使武鄕鎭使安居受潛以蠟丸乞師於李克用，請復軍府於潞州。

translations.literal: Army supervisor Qi Shenhui, because people's hearts were unsettled, sent Wuxiang post commissioner An Jushou secretly with a wax-sealed ball to beg troops from Li Keyong, requesting restore the military headquarters at Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Army Supervisor Qi Shenhui, seeing popular unrest, had the Wuxiang post commissioner An Jushou smuggle a wax-sealed plea to Li Keyong asking for troops to restore the military headquarters at Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，克用遣其將賀公雅等赴之，爲方立所敗；

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, Keyong dispatched his generals He Gongya and others to go to their aid; they were defeated by Fangli;
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, Li Keyong sent He Gongya and other generals to Luzhou, but Meng Fangli defeated them.

sentences.zh: 又遣李克脩擊之，辛亥，取潞州，殺其刺史李殷銳。

translations.literal: Again he dispatched Li Kexiu to attack them; on the day xinhai he took Luzhou and killed its prefect Li Yinrui.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent Li Kexiu, who on the day xinhai took Luzhou and killed the prefect Li Yinrui.

sentences.zh: 是後克用每歲出兵爭山東，三州之人半爲俘馘，野無稼穡矣。

translations.literal: After this Keyong every year sent troops to contest Shandong; people of the three prefectures half became captives and heads; in the wilds no grain crops.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Li Keyong raided east of the mountains every year. Half the population of the three prefectures was killed or captured, and the fields lay untilled.

sentences.zh: 以宗女爲安化長公主，妻南詔。

translations.literal: An imperial clan daughter was made Princess Chang of Anhua and married to Nanzhao.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial daughter was made Princess Chang of Anhua and sent to marry the king of Nanzhao.

sentences.zh: 劉漢宏將十餘萬眾出西陵，將擊董昌；

translations.literal: Liu Hanhong led more than 100,000 masses out through Xiling, about to attack Dong Chang;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hanhong marched more than a hundred thousand men through Xiling Pass to strike Dong Chang.

sentences.zh: 戊午，錢鏐濟江逆戰，大破之，漢宏易服持鱠刀而遁。

translations.literal: On the day wuwu, Qian Liu crossed the river to meet in battle and greatly defeated them; Hanhong changed clothes, took a kitchen knife, and fled.
translations.idiomatic: On the day wuwu, Qian Liu crossed the river to meet him and routed his army. Liu Hanhong disguised himself, seized a kitchen knife, and fled.

sentences.zh: 己未，漢宏收餘眾四萬又戰，鏐又破之，斬其弟漢容及將辛約。

translations.literal: On the day jiwei, Hanhong gathered remaining troops of forty thousand and fought again; Liu again defeated them and beheaded his younger brother Hanrong and general Xin Yue.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiwei, Liu Hanhong regrouped forty thousand survivors and fought again. Qian Liu defeated him once more, killing his brother Hanrong and the general Xin Yue.

sentences.zh: 十一月，甲子朔，秦宗權圍許州。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, first day of month jiazi, Qin Zongquan besieged Xu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on the new moon of the day jiazi, Qin Zongquan besieged Xu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 忠武大將鹿晏弘帥所部自河中南掠襄、鄧、金、洋，所過屠滅，聲雲西赴行在。

translations.literal: Zhongwu great general Lu Yanhong led his command from south of the river in plunder through Xiang, Deng, Jin, and Yang; wherever they passed, slaughter and extinction; he proclaimed going west to the mobile court.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yanhong, a senior general of Zhongwu, led his men south of the Yellow River in a sweep through Xiang, Deng, Jin, and Yang, leaving slaughter wherever they passed while announcing that he was marching west to join the emperor.

sentences.zh: 十二月，至興元，逐節度使牛勖，勖奔龍州西山。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, he reached Xingyuan, expelled Military Commissioner Niu Xu; Xu fled to the western mountains of Long Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he reached Xingyuan, drove out Military Commissioner Niu Xu, who fled into the western hills of Long Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 晏弘據興元，自稱留後。

translations.literal: Yanhong seized Xingyuan and proclaimed himself regent.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yanhong seized Xingyuan and proclaimed himself acting military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 感化節度使時溥因食中毒，疑判官李凝古而殺之。

translations.literal: Ganhua Military Commissioner Shi Pu, because of food poisoning, suspected his aide Li Ninggu and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Pu, military commissioner of Ganhua, suffered food poisoning, suspected his aide Li Ninggu of poisoning him, and had him killed.

sentences.zh: 凝古父損，爲右散騎常侍，在成都，溥奏凝古與父同謀。

translations.literal: Ninggu's father Sun was right Gentlemen-at-Large Cavalier Attendant at Chengdu; Pu memorialized that Ninggu and his father plotted together.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ninggu's father Li Sun, a right Gentlemen-at-Large Cavalier Attendant, was in Chengdu. Shi Pu accused father and son of conspiring together.

sentences.zh: 田令孜受溥賂，令御史台鞫之。

translations.literal: Tian Lingzi accepted Pu's bribe and ordered the Censorate to interrogate.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Lingzi accepted Shi Pu's bribe and ordered the Censorate to investigate.

sentences.zh: 侍卸史王華爲損論冤，令孜矯詔移損下神策獄，華拒而不遣。

translations.literal: Attending censor Wang Hua argued innocence for Sun; Lingzi forged an edict to transfer Sun down to Shence prison; Hua refused and did not send him.
translations.idiomatic: Attending Censor Wang Hua pleaded Li Sun's innocence. Tian Lingzi forged an edict to move Sun into Shence custody, but Wang Hua refused to hand him over.

sentences.zh: 蕭遘奏：「李凝古行毒，事出暖昧，已爲溥所殺，父損相別數年，聲問不通，安得誣以同謀！

translations.literal: Xiao Xu memorialized: "Li Ninggu committed poisoning; the matter is obscure, and he has already been killed by Pu; father Sun have been apart for several years with no communication; how can they be falsely charged with plotting together!
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Xu memorialized: "Li Ninggu's poisoning charge was murky to begin with, and Shi Pu has already killed him. Father and son have been separated for years without contact—how can they be accused of conspiracy?

sentences.zh: 溥恃功亂法，陵蔑朝廷，欲殺天子侍臣；

translations.literal: Pu relies on merit to violate law and insult the court, wishing to kill the emperor's attendant officials;
translations.idiomatic: Shi Pu abuses his battlefield merit to defy the law and bully the court, and now seeks to kill the emperor's own attendants.

sentences.zh: 若徇其欲，行及臣輩，朝廷何以自立！」

translations.literal: if his desire is indulged, it will reach even us ministers; how can the court stand!"
translations.idiomatic: If this is granted, it will reach us next—how can the court endure it?"

sentences.zh: 由是損得免死，歸田裡。

translations.literal: Thus Sun was spared death and returned to his fields.
translations.idiomatic: Li Sun was spared execution and sent home to his estate.

sentences.zh: 時令孜專權，群臣莫敢迕視，惟遘屢與爭辯，朝廷倚之。

translations.literal: At the time Lingzi monopolized power; ministers dared not meet his gaze; only Xu repeatedly argued with him; the court relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Lingzi then held unchecked power and few ministers dared cross him. Xiao Xu alone argued with him again and again, and the court leaned on him.

sentences.zh: 升浙東爲義勝軍，以劉漢宏爲節度使。

translations.literal: Zhedong was promoted to Yisheng Army; Liu Hanhong was made military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Zhedong was elevated to the Yisheng circuit, and Liu Hanhong was appointed its military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 趙犨遣人間道求救於鄰道，於是周岌、時溥、朱全忠皆引兵救之。

translations.literal: Zhao Chou sent men by secret route to beg rescue from neighboring circuits; thereupon Zhou Ji, Shi Pu, and Zhu Quanzhong all led troops to rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Chou sent envoys by hidden routes to beg aid from neighboring circuits. Zhou Ji, Shi Pu, and Zhu Quanzhong all marched to relieve him.

sentences.zh: 全忠與黃巢之黨戰於鹿邑，敗之，斬首二千餘級，遂引兵入亳州而據之。

translations.literal: Quanzhong battled Huang Chao's partisans at Luyi, defeated them, beheaded more than two thousand, then led troops into Bozhou and seized it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong fought Huang Chao's followers at Luyi, routed them, and took more than two thousand heads, then advanced into Bozhou and occupied it.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，以鹿晏弘爲興元留後。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, Lu Yanhong was made Xingyuan regent.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, Lu Yanhong was confirmed as acting military commissioner of Xingyuan.

sentences.zh: 賜魏博節度使樂行達名彥禎。

translations.literal: Weibo Military Commissioner Yue Xingda was granted the name Yan Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Xingda, military commissioner of Weibo, was granted the personal name Yan Zhen.

sentences.zh: 東川節度使楊師立以陳敬瑄兄弟權寵之盛，心不能平。

translations.literal: Dongchuan Military Commissioner Yang Shili, because the Chen Jingxuan brothers' power and favor were excessive, in his heart could not be at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Shili of Dongchuan could not stomach the Chen Jingxuan brothers' grip on favor and power.

sentences.zh: 敬瑄之遣高仁厚討韓秀升也，語之曰：「成功而還，當奏天子，以東川相賞。」

translations.literal: When Jingxuan sent Gao Renhou to attack Han Xiuzheng, he told him: "If you succeed and return, I shall memorialize the Son of Heaven and reward you with Dongchuan."
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Jingxuan sent Gao Renhou against Han Xiuzheng, he told him: "Return victorious and I will petition the throne to give you Dongchuan as your reward."

sentences.zh: 師立聞之，怒曰：「彼此列籓，而遽以我疆土許人，是無天地也！」

translations.literal: Shili heard this and angrily said: "We are both frontier commissioners, yet you rashly promise my territory to another—this is to know no bounds!"
translations.idiomatic: Yang Shili heard of it and raged: "We are fellow frontier commissioners, yet you casually offer my domain to someone else—as if heaven and earth meant nothing!"

sentences.zh: 田令孜恐其爲亂，因其不發兵遏，征師立爲右僕射。

translations.literal: Tian Lingzi feared he would make trouble; because he did not send troops to block the rebels, Shili was summoned as right vice director.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Lingzi, fearing he would rebel, recalled him to court as right vice director because he had failed to block the rebels.

sentences.zh: 黃巢兵尚強，周岌、時溥、朱全忠不能支，共求救於河東節度使李克用。

translations.literal: Huang Chao's troops were still strong; Zhou Ji, Shi Pu, and Zhu Quanzhong could not hold them; together they begged rescue from Hedong Military Commissioner Li Keyong.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Chao's army was still formidable. Zhou Ji, Shi Pu, and Zhu Quanzhong could not hold the line and jointly begged Li Keyong of Hedong for help.

sentences.zh: 二月，克用將蕃、漢兵五萬出天井關，河陽節度使諸葛爽辭以河橋不完，屯兵萬善以拒之。

translations.literal: Second month, Keyong led fifty thousand Tangut and Han troops out through Tianjing Pass; Heyang Military Commissioner Zhuge Shuang declined on the grounds that the He Bridge was unfinished and massed ten thousand troops at Wanshan to block him.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Li Keyong marched fifty thousand Tangut and Han troops through Tianjing Pass. Zhuge Shuang of Heyang refused passage, claiming the Yellow River bridge was unfinished, and massed ten thousand men at Wanshan to block him.

sentences.zh: 克用乃還兵自陝、河中渡河而東。

translations.literal: Keyong then turned his army back and crossed the river by the Shaan and Hezhong route to go east.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong swung south, crossed the Yellow River through Shaan and Hezhong, and marched east.

sentences.zh: 楊師立得詔書，怒，不受代，殺官告使及監軍使，舉兵，以討陳敬瑄爲名，大將有諫者輒殺之，進屯涪城，遣其將郝蠲襲綿州，不克。

translations.literal: Yang Shili received the edict, was angry, refused to accept replacement, killed the credential envoy and army supervisor, raised troops, taking attack on Chen Jingxuan as his name; great generals who remonstrated were at once killed; he advanced and encamped at Fucheng, sent his general Hao Juan to raid Mian Prefecture, but could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Shili received the recall, flew into a rage, and refused to step down. He killed the credential bearer and the army supervisor, took up arms in the name of punishing Chen Jingxuan, and executed any senior officer who objected. He advanced to Fucheng and sent Hao Juan against Mian Prefecture without success.

sentences.zh: 丙午，以陳敬瑄爲西川、東川、山南西道都指揮、招討、安撫、處置等使。

translations.literal: On the day bingwu, Chen Jingxuan was made overall commander, punitive commissioner, pacification commissioner, and disposition commissioner of Xichuan, Dongchuan, and Shannan West.
translations.idiomatic: On the day bingwu Chen Jingxuan was made overall commander, punitive commissioner, pacification commissioner, and disposition commissioner of Xichuan, Dongchuan, and Shannan West.

sentences.zh: 三月，甲子，楊師立移檄行在百官及諸道將吏士庶，數陳敬瑄十罪，自言集本道將士、八州壇丁共十五萬人，長驅問罪。

translations.literal: Third month, day jiazi, Yang Shili issued a proclamation to the mobile court's hundred officials and to generals, officials, soldiers, and commoners of all circuits, enumerating Chen Jingxuan's ten crimes, declaring himself to have gathered this circuit's generals and soldiers and altar levies of eight prefectures totaling 150,000 men, to drive straight and demand punishment.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on the day jiazi, Yang Shili circulated a proclamation to the court in exile and to officers and civilians of every circuit, listing ten crimes of Chen Jingxuan and claiming an army of 150,000 drawn from his circuit's troops and ritual levies across eight prefectures, ready to march in force for justice.

sentences.zh: 詔削師立官爵，以眉州防禦使高仁厚爲東川留後，將兵五千討之，以西川押牙楊茂言爲行軍副使。

translations.literal: An edict stripped Shili of rank and office; Meizhou defense commissioner Gao Renhou was made Dongchuan regent; he led five thousand troops to attack him, with Xichuan commandant Yang Maoyan as campaign deputy.
translations.idiomatic: An edict stripped Yang Shili of rank and title. Gao Renhou, defense commissioner of Meizhou, was made acting commissioner of Dongchuan and sent with five thousand men against him, with Yang Maoyan of Xichuan as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 朱全忠擊黃巢瓦子寨，拔之；

translations.literal: Zhu Quanzhong attacked Huang Chao's Wazi Stockade and took it;
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong stormed Huang Chao's Wazi Stockade and captured it;

sentences.zh: 巢將陝人李唐賓、楚丘王虔裕降於全忠。

translations.literal: Chao's generals Li Tangbin of Shaan and Wang Qianyu of Chuqiu surrendered to Quanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Chao's generals Li Tangbin of Shaan and Wang Qianyu of Chuqiu surrendered to Zhu Quanzhong.

sentences.zh: 婺州人王鎭執刺史黃碣，降於錢鏐。

translations.literal: Wuzhou man Wang Zhen seized Prefect Huang Jie and surrendered to Qian Liu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhen of Wuzhou seized Prefect Huang Jie and submitted to Qian Liu.

sentences.zh: 劉漢宏遣其將婁賚殺鎭而代之，浦陽鎭將蔣環召鏐兵共攻婺州，擒賚而還。

translations.literal: Liu Hanhong sent his general Lou Ben to kill Zhen and replace him; Puyang post commander Jiang Huan summoned Liu's troops to attack Wuzhou together, captured Ben, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hanhong sent Lou Ben to kill Wang Zhen and take his place. Jiang Huan, commander of the Puyang post, called in Qian Liu's troops to assault Wuzhou, captured Lou Ben, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 碣，閩人也。

translations.literal: Jie was a man of Min.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Jie was a native of Min.

sentences.zh: 高駢從子左驍衞大將軍澞，疏呂用之罪狀二十餘幅，密以呈駢，且泣曰：「用之內則假神仙之説，蠱惑尊聽；

translations.literal: Gao Pian's nephew, Left Brave Guards great general Yu, submitted a memorial of more than twenty sheets detailing Lü Yongzhi's crimes, secretly presenting it to Pian, and weeping said: "Yongzhi inwardly uses the talk of immortals to bewitch and delude your honored hearing;
translations.idiomatic: Gao Pian's nephew Gao Yu, a senior general of the Left Brave Guards, drafted more than twenty sheets listing Lü Yongzhi's crimes and secretly handed them to Pian, weeping as he said: "Inwardly Yongzhi uses talk of immortals to bewitch your judgment;

sentences.zh: 外則盜節制之權，殘賊百姓；

translations.literal: outwardly he usurps the power of command and cruelly harms the common people;
translations.idiomatic: outwardly he steals command authority and brutalizes the people;

sentences.zh: 將佐懼死，莫之敢言。

translations.literal: staff and generals fear death; none dare speak.
translations.idiomatic: your officers fear for their lives and dare not speak.

sentences.zh: 歲月浸深，羽翼將成，苟不除之，恐高氏弈代勳庸，一朝掃地矣！」

translations.literal: As months and years deepen, his wings will be formed; if he is not removed, I fear the Gao clan's merit across generations will in one morning be swept to the ground!"
translations.idiomatic: Month by month his power grows. Unless he is removed, the Gao family's generations of merit may be swept away overnight!"

sentences.zh: 因嗚咽不自勝。

translations.literal: He then sobbed uncontrollably.
translations.idiomatic: He broke down sobbing.

sentences.zh: 駢曰：「汝醉邪！」

translations.literal: Pian said: "Are you drunk!
translations.idiomatic: Gao Pian said, "Are you drunk?"

sentences.zh: 命扶出。

translations.literal: He ordered attendants to help him out.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered attendants to help him out.

sentences.zh: 明日，以澞狀示用之，用之曰：「四十郎嘗以空乏見告，未獲遵命，故有此憾。」

translations.literal: The next day he showed Yu's memorial to Yongzhi; Yongzhi said: "Forty Lang once complained to me of being destitute; I did not yet carry out his request, so he bears this resentment."
translations.idiomatic: The next day he showed Yu's memorial to Lü Yongzhi. Yongzhi said, "Forty Lang once begged me for funds I had not yet granted—hence this grudge."

sentences.zh: 因出澞手書數幅呈之。

translations.literal: He then produced several sheets in Yu's own hand and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: He produced several letters in Yu's own hand and showed them to Pian.

sentences.zh: 駢甚慚，遂禁澞出入；

translations.literal: Pian was greatly ashamed and therefore barred Yu from going in and out;
translations.idiomatic: Gao Pian was deeply shamed and forbade Yu to come and go;

sentences.zh: 後月餘，以澞知舒州事。

translations.literal: more than a month later, Yu was made to administer Shuzhou affairs.
translations.idiomatic: and a month later appointed him to govern Shuzhou.

sentences.zh: 群盜陳儒攻舒州，澞求救於廬州。

translations.literal: Bandit Chen Ru attacked Shuzhou; Yu begged rescue from Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The bandit Chen Ru attacked Shuzhou, and Yu begged Yang Xingmin in Luzhou for aid.

sentences.zh: 楊行愍力不能救，謀於其將李神福，神福請不用寸刃而逐之。

translations.literal: Yang Xingmin by strength could not save him; he consulted his general Li Shenfu; Shenfu requested not to use a single blade to drive them off.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xingmin lacked the strength to rescue him and consulted his general Li Shenfu, who said he needed no weapon to expel the enemy.

sentences.zh: 乃多繼旗幟，間道入舒州，頃之，引舒州兵建廬州旗幟而出，指畫地形，若布大陳狀；

translations.literal: He then added many flags and banners, entered Shuzhou by a hidden route; shortly he led Shuzhou troops bearing Luzhou flags and banners out, pointing and tracing terrain as if deploying a great battle array;
translations.idiomatic: Li Shenfu raised many extra banners and slipped into Shuzhou by a back road. Soon he marched Shuzhou troops out under Luzhou colors, gesturing over the ground as if laying out a great battle line.

sentences.zh: 賊懼，宵遁。

translations.literal: the bandits were afraid and fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: The raiders panicked and fled overnight.

sentences.zh: 神福，洺州人也。

translations.literal: Shenfu was a man of Luozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shenfu was a native of Luozhou.

sentences.zh: 久之，群盜呉迥、李本復攻舒州，澞不能守，棄城走，駢使人就殺之。

translations.literal: After a long time, bandits Wu Hui and Li Ben again attacked Shuzhou; Yu could not hold it, abandoned the city and fled; Pian sent men to go kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward the bandits Wu Hui and Li Ben attacked Shuzhou again. Yu could not hold the city, fled, and Gao Pian had him hunted down and killed.

sentences.zh: 楊行愍遣其將合肥陶雅、清流張訓等將兵擊呉迥、李本，擒斬之，以雅攝州刺史。

translations.literal: Yang Xingmin sent his generals Tao Ya of Hefei and Zhang Xun of Qingliu with troops to attack Wu Hui and Li Ben, captured and beheaded them, and made Ya acting prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xingmin sent Tao Ya of Hefei and Zhang Xun of Qingliu against Wu Hui and Li Ben, captured and executed them, and made Tao Ya acting prefect.

sentences.zh: 秦宗權遣其弟將兵寇廬州，據舒城，楊行愍遣其將合肥田頵擊走之。

translations.literal: Qin Zongquan sent his younger brother with troops to raid Luzhou, seized Shucheng; Yang Xingmin sent his general Tian Jun of Hefei to attack and drive them off.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Zongquan sent his brother to raid Luzhou and seize Shucheng. Yang Xingmin sent Tian Jun of Hefei to beat them back.

sentences.zh: 前杭州刺史路審中客居黃州，聞鄂州刺史崔紹卒，募兵三千人入據之。

translations.literal: Former Hangzhou prefect Lu Shenzhong, living as a guest at Huang Prefecture, heard that E Prefecture prefect Cui Shao had died, raised three thousand troops and entered to seize it.
translations.idiomatic: Former Hangzhou Prefect Lu Shenzhong, living in exile at Huang Prefecture, heard that Prefect Cui Shao of Ezhou had died, raised three thousand men, and seized the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 武昌牙將杜洪亦逐岳州刺史而代之。

translations.literal: Wuchang garrison officer Du Hong also expelled the Yuezhou prefect and replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: Du Hong, a Wuchang garrison officer, likewise drove out the prefect of Yuezhou and took his place.

sentences.zh: 黃巢圍陳州幾三百日，趙犨兄弟與之大小數百戰，雖兵食將盡，而眾心益固。

translations.literal: Huang Chao besieged Chen Prefecture for nearly three hundred days; the Zhao Chou brothers with him fought great and small battles numbering in the hundreds; although troops and food were nearly exhausted, popular hearts grew firmer.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Chao had besieged Chen Prefecture for nearly three hundred days. The Zhao Chou brothers fought him in hundreds of engagements. Though supplies and manpower were nearly gone, the defenders' resolve only hardened.

sentences.zh: 李克用會許、汴、徐、兗之軍於陳州。

translations.literal: Li Keyong joined the armies of Xu, Bian, Xuzhou, and Yan at Chen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong united the armies of Xu, Bian, Xuzhou, and Yan at Chen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時尚讓屯太康，夏，四月，癸巳，諸軍進拔太康。

translations.literal: At the time Shang Rang was encamped at Taikang; summer, fourth month, day guisi, the allied armies advanced and took Taikang.
translations.idiomatic: Shang Rang was then encamped at Taikang. In summer, the fourth month, on the day guisi, the allied armies advanced and captured Taikang.

sentences.zh: 黃思鄴屯西華，諸軍復攻之。

translations.literal: Huang Siye was encamped at Xihua; the allied armies again attacked him.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Siye held Xihua, and the allies attacked him there as well.

sentences.zh: 思鄴走。

translations.literal: Siye fled.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Siye fled.

sentences.zh: 黃巢聞之懼，退軍故陽裡，陳州圍始解。

translations.literal: Huang Chao heard this and was afraid; he withdrew his army to Guyangli; the siege of Chen Prefecture was then lifted.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Chao heard the news and panicked. He pulled back to Guyangli, and the siege of Chen Prefecture was finally broken.

sentences.zh: 朱全忠聞黃巢將至，引軍還大梁。

translations.literal: Zhu Quanzhong heard Huang Chao was about to arrive, led army back to Great Liang.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Quanzhong learned that Huang Chao was approaching, he withdrew his army to Great Liang.

sentences.zh: 五月，癸亥，大雨，平地三尺，黃巢營爲水所漂，且聞李克用至，遂引兵東北趣汴州，屠尉氏。

translations.literal: Fifth month, day guihai, great rain, level ground three chi, Huang Chao's camp was floated away by water, and hearing Li Keyong had arrived, then led troops northeast toward Bian Prefecture, slaughtered Weishi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on the day guihai, torrential rain raised the water three feet deep across the plain. Huang Chao's camp was washed away, and when word came that Li Keyong was near, he marched northeast toward Bian Prefecture and massacred Weishi.

sentences.zh: 尚讓以驍騎五千進逼大梁，至於繁台，宣武將豐人朱珍、南華龐師古擊卻之。

translations.literal: Shang Rang with five thousand fierce cavalry pressed Great Liang, reaching Fantai; Xuanwu generals Feng native Zhu Zhen, Nanhua Pang Shigu attacked and repelled them.
translations.idiomatic: Shang Rang advanced on Great Liang with five thousand elite horsemen as far as Fantai, but Zhu Zhen of Feng and Pang Shigu of Nanhua, generals of Xuanwu, drove them back.

sentences.zh: 全忠復告急於李克用。

translations.literal: Quanzhong again reported urgency to Li Keyong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong again urgently appealed to Li Keyong for help.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，克用與忠武都監使田從異發許州，戊辰，追及黃巢於中牟北王滿渡，乘其半濟，奮擊，大破之，殺萬餘人，賊遂潰。

translations.literal: On day bingyin, Keyong with Zhongwu army overseer Tian Congyi set out from Xu Prefecture; on day wuchen, overtook Huang Chao at north of Zhongmou at Wangman Ford, took advantage of his half crossing, fiercely attacked, greatly broke them, killed more than ten thousand; rebels then routed.
translations.idiomatic: On the day bingyin, Li Keyong and Tian Congyi, army overseer of Zhongwu, marched out from Xu Prefecture. On the day wuchen he caught Huang Chao at Wangman Ford north of Zhongmou, struck while the rebels were half across the river, routed them utterly, and killed more than ten thousand. The rebel army disintegrated.

sentences.zh: 尚讓帥其眾降時溥，別將臨晉李讜、曲周霍存、甄城葛從周、冤句張歸霸及從弟歸厚帥其眾降朱全忠。

translations.literal: Shang Rang led his masses to surrender to Shi Pu; separate generals Linjin Li Dan, Quzhou Huo Cun, Zhencheng Ge Congzhou, Yuanqu Zhang Guiba and younger cousin Guihou led their masses to surrender to Zhu Quanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Shang Rang surrendered with his following to Shi Pu. The detachment commanders Li Dan of Linjin, Huo Cun of Quzhou, Ge Congzhou of Zhencheng, Zhang Guiba of Yuanqu, and Zhang's younger cousin Guihou each submitted their troops to Zhu Quanzhong.

sentences.zh: 巢逾汴而北，己巳，克用追擊之於封丘，又破之。

translations.literal: Chao crossed Bian and went north; on day jisi, Keyong pursued and attacked at Fengqiu, again broke them.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Chao crossed north of the Bian River. On the day jisi Li Keyong caught him at Fengqiu and defeated him again.

sentences.zh: 庚午夜，復大雨，賊驚懼東走，克用追之，過胙城、匡城。

translations.literal: On night of day gengwu, again great rain; rebels frightened and fled east; Keyong pursued, passed Zuocheng, Kuangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: At midnight on the day gengwu another downpour fell. Panic-stricken, the rebels fled eastward. Li Keyong pursued them through Zuocheng and Kuangcheng.

sentences.zh: 巢收餘眾近千人，東奔充州。

translations.literal: Chao gathered remnant masses nearly a thousand, east fled toward Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Chao mustered fewer than a thousand survivors and fled east toward Yan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 辛未，克用追至冤句，騎能屬者才數百人，晝夜行二百餘里，人馬疲乏，糧盡，乃還汴州，欲裹糧復追之，獲巢幼子及乘輿器服符印，得所掠男女萬人，悉縱遣之。

translations.literal: On day xinwei, Keyong pursued to Yuanqu; horsemen able to follow were only several hundred; day and night marched more than two hundred li; men and horses exhausted, grain exhausted, then returned to Bian Prefecture, wished to wrap grain and again pursue; obtained Chao's young son and imperial carriage utensils robes seals, got men and women plundered ten thousand, all released and sent away.
translations.idiomatic: On the day xinwei Li Keyong chased Huang Chao as far as Yuanqu, but only a few hundred horsemen could keep pace. They had ridden more than two hundred li without rest; men and mounts were spent and provisions gone. He turned back to Bian Prefecture, intending to resupply and resume the pursuit. He captured Huang Chao's young son along with imperial regalia, seals, and ceremonial vessels, and recovered ten thousand captive men and women, whom he released and sent home.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，高仁厚屯德陽，楊師立遣其將鄭君雄、張士安據鹿頭關以拒之。

translations.literal: On day guiyou, Gao Renhou encamped at Deyang; Yang Shili sent his generals Zheng Junxiong, Zhang Shi'an to hold Lutou Pass to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: On the day guiyou, Gao Renhou camped at Deyang. Yang Shili sent Zheng Junxiong and Zhang Shi'an to hold Lutou Pass against him.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，李克用至汴州，營於城外，朱全忠固請入城，館於上源驛。

translations.literal: On day jiaxu, Li Keyong arrived at Bian Prefecture, encamped outside the city; Zhu Quanzhong firmly invited him into the city, lodged at Shangyuan Post.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiaxu, Li Keyong reached Bian Prefecture and pitched camp outside the walls. Zhu Quanzhong pressed him to enter the city and lodged him at Shangyuan Post.

sentences.zh: 全忠就置酒、聲樂，饌具皆精豐，禮貌甚恭。

translations.literal: Quanzhong thereupon set out wine, music; feast items all refined and abundant, courtesy very respectful.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong entertained him with wine and music, serving a lavish and elegant banquet with every show of respect.

sentences.zh: 克用乘酒使氣，語頗侵之，全忠不平，薄暮，罷酒，從者皆沾醉，宣武將楊彥洪密與全忠謀，連車樹柵以塞衢路，發兵圍驛而攻之，呼聲動地。

translations.literal: Keyong riding wine vented temper, words quite encroached on him; Quanzhong was displeased; toward dusk, wine ended, followers all thoroughly drunk; Xuanwu general Yang Yanhong secretly with Quanzhong plotted, linked carts planted palisades to block streets, sent troops to surround the post and attack, cries shook the earth.
translations.idiomatic: Emboldened by wine, Li Keyong grew overbearing and his words turned insulting. Zhu Quanzhong took offense. At dusk the banquet broke up, his escort dead drunk. The Xuanwu officer Yang Yanhong secretly plotted with Zhu Quanzhong: they chained wagons and raised barricades to seal the streets, then sent soldiers to surround the post. The din of battle shook the ground.

sentences.zh: 克用醉，不之聞；

translations.literal: Keyong was drunk, did not hear it;
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong, drunk, heard nothing;

sentences.zh: 親兵薛志勤、史敬思等十餘人格鬥，侍者郭景銖滅燭，扶克用匿床下，以水沃其面，徐告以難，克用始張目援弓而起。

translations.literal: Personal soldiers Xue Zhiqin, Shi Jingsi and more than ten others fought hand to hand; attendant Guo Jingzhu extinguished candles, supported Keyong hiding under the bed, poured water on his face, slowly told of the crisis; Keyong then opened eyes, took bow and rose.
translations.idiomatic: but a dozen of his personal guards, including Xue Zhiqin and Shi Jingsi, fought hand to hand. The attendant Guo Jingzhu snuffed the lamps, pulled Li Keyong under the bed, splashed water on his face, and slowly told him of the attack. Li Keyong opened his eyes, seized his bow, and rose.

sentences.zh: 志勤射汴人，死者數十。

translations.literal: Zhiqin shot Bian men, dead several tens.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Zhiqin shot down dozens of the men from Bian.

sentences.zh: 須臾，煙火四合，會大雨震電，天地晦冥，志勤扶克用帥左右數人，逾坦突圍，乘電光而行，汴人扼橋，力戰得度，史敬思爲後拒，戰死。

translations.literal: In a moment, smoke and fire closed on all sides; it happened great rain thundered and lightning, heaven and earth dark; Zhiqin supported Keyong leading several men on the left and right, over wall broke encirclement, riding lightning went; Bian men held the bridge, fought hard and crossed; Shi Jingsi as rear guard, fought and died.
translations.idiomatic: Soon smoke and flame closed in on every side. Thunder and lightning lashed the sky in a torrential rain until heaven and earth were black. Xue Zhiqin guided Li Keyong and a few companions over the wall and through the encirclement, advancing by flashes of lightning. The men of Bian held the bridge, but after a fierce fight they forced their way across. Shi Jingsi covered the retreat and was killed in action.

sentences.zh: 克用登尉氏門，縋城得出，監軍陳景思等三百餘人，皆爲汴人所殺。

translations.literal: Keyong ascended Weishi Gate, lowered by rope over wall and got out; army overseer Chen Jingsi and more than three hundred, all were killed by Bian men.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong climbed Weishi Gate and was let down by rope from the wall to escape. Chen Jingsi, his army overseer, and more than three hundred others were all slain by the men of Bian.

sentences.zh: 楊彥洪謂全忠曰：「胡人急則乘馬，見乘馬者則射之。」

translations.literal: Yang Yanhong told Quanzhong saying: "When barbarians are urgent they mount horses; seeing one who mounts a horse, then shoot him.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yanhong told Zhu Quanzhong, "When these barbarians panic they take to horseback. Shoot anyone you see on a horse.

sentences.zh: 是夕，彥洪乘馬適在全忠前，全忠射之，殪。

translations.literal: That evening, Yanhong mounted horse just before Quanzhong; Quanzhong shot him, killed.
translations.idiomatic: That night Yang Yanhong rode up directly in front of Zhu Quanzhong, and Zhu Quanzhong shot him dead.

sentences.zh: 克用妻劉氏，多智略，左右先脫歸者以汴人爲變告，劉氏神色不動，立斬之，陰召大將約束，謀保軍以還。

translations.literal: Keyong's wife Lady Liu, much wisdom and stratagem; attendants who first escaped and returned reported Bian men had mutinied; Lady Liu's expression did not move, immediately beheaded them, secretly summoned great generals to impose discipline, planned to preserve army and return.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong's wife Lady Liu was a woman of keen intelligence. Attendants who had escaped first came back with word of treachery at Bian. Lady Liu did not flinch; she had them executed on the spot, secretly summoned the senior commanders to hold the ranks together, and planned how to withdraw the army safely.

sentences.zh: 比明，克用至，欲勒兵攻全忠，劉氏曰：「公比爲國討賊，救東諸侯之急，今汴人不道，乃謀害公，自當訴之朝廷。

translations.literal: When dawn came, Keyong arrived, wished to marshal troops to attack Quanzhong; Lady Liu said: "Your Lordship lately for the state punished rebels, rescued eastern feudatories' urgency; now Bian men are without the Way, yet plotted to harm Your Lordship—you should naturally appeal to the court.
translations.idiomatic: At daybreak Li Keyong arrived and wanted to march against Zhu Quanzhong. Lady Liu said, "You have been fighting the rebels for the empire and relieving the eastern lords in their distress. The men of Bian have committed a crime by plotting your murder—you should lay the case before the court.

sentences.zh: 若擅舉兵相攻，則天下孰能辨其曲直！

translations.literal: If on your own authority you raise troops to attack each other, then under heaven who can distinguish right and wrong!
translations.idiomatic: If you take up arms on your own, who under heaven will be able to tell right from wrong?

sentences.zh: 且彼得以有辭矣。」

translations.literal: Moreover they will obtain grounds for argument.
translations.idiomatic: You will only give them a pretext.

sentences.zh: 克用從之，引兵去，但移書責全忠。

translations.literal: Keyong followed this, led troops away, only sent letter rebuking Quanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong agreed, withdrew his army, and merely sent a letter rebuking Zhu Quanzhong.

sentences.zh: 全忠復書曰：「前夕之變，僕不之知，朝廷自遣使者與楊彥洪爲謀，彥洪既伏其辜，惟公諒察。」

translations.literal: Quanzhong replied saying: "The change of the other evening, I did not know of it; the court itself sent envoys to plot with Yang Yanhong; Yanhong has already paid his crime, only pray Your Lordship understand."
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong wrote back, "I knew nothing of what happened the other night. The court itself sent envoys to plot with Yang Yanhong. He has paid for his crime. I beg your understanding."

sentences.zh: 克用養子嗣源，年十七，從克用自上源山，矢石之間，獨無所傷。

translations.literal: Keyong's adopted son Siyuan, age seventeen, followed Keyong from Shangyuan, amid arrows and stones, alone had no injury.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong's adopted son Li Siyuan, seventeen years old, accompanied him away from Shangyuan. Though arrows and stones flew thick around them, he alone came through unhurt.

sentences.zh: 嗣源本胡人，名邈佶烈，無姓。

translations.literal: Siyuan originally was a barbarian, name Yaojilie, no surname.
translations.idiomatic: Siyuan was originally a barbarian named Yaojilie and had no clan name.

sentences.zh: 克用擇軍中驍勇者，多養爲子，名回鶻張政之子曰存信，振武孫重進曰存進，許州王賢曰存賢，安敬思曰存孝，皆冒姓李氏。

translations.literal: Keyong selected fierce brave in the army, many raised as sons, named: Huigu Zhang Zheng's son called Cunxin, Zhenwu Sun Chongjin called Cunjin, Xuzhou Wang Xian called Cunxian, An Jingsi called Cunxiao, all falsely surnamed Li.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong took the bravest men in his army and adopted many as sons: Zhang Zheng the Huigu's son he named Cunxin; Sun Chongjin of Zhenwu he named Cunjin; Wang Xian of Xuzhou he named Cunxian; An Jingsi he named Cunxiao. All took the surname Li.

sentences.zh: 丙子，克用至許州故寨，求糧於周岌，岌辭以糧乏，乃自陝濟河還晉陽。

translations.literal: On day bingzi, Keyong reached Xu Prefecture old camp, sought grain from Zhou Ji; Ji declined citing grain scarcity, then from Shaan crossed river and returned to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: On the day bingzi, Li Keyong reached his old camp at Xu Prefecture and asked Zhou Ji for provisions. Zhou pleaded scarcity. Li Keyong crossed the Yellow River from Shaanxi and returned to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 鄭君雄、張士安堅壁不出，高仁厚曰：「攻之則彼利我傷，圍之則彼困我逸。」

translations.literal: Zheng Junxiong, Zhang Shi'an fortified walls and did not come out; Gao Renhou said: "If we attack, they profit and we are wounded; if we besiege, they are trapped and we are at ease."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Junxiong and Zhang Shi'an held their walls and refused battle. Gao Renhou said, "If we attack, they gain and we suffer. If we besiege, they grow desperate while we rest easy."

sentences.zh: 遂列十二寨圍之。

translations.literal: Then he arrayed twelve camps to surround them.
translations.idiomatic: He then pitched twelve camps and invested the place.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，夜二鼓，君雄等出勁兵掩擊城北副使寨，楊茂言不能御，帥眾棄寨走，其旁數寨見副使走，亦走。

translations.literal: On day dingchou, at night second drum, Junxiong and others sent fierce troops to secretly attack the north of the city deputy commander's camp; Yang Maoyan could not resist, led masses abandoned camp and fled; several neighboring camps seeing deputy flee, also fled.
translations.idiomatic: On the day dingchou, at the second watch, Zheng Junxiong sent elite troops in a surprise strike against the northern deputy commander's camp. Yang Maoyan could not hold and fled with his men. When the neighboring camps saw the deputy commander run, they fled as well.

sentences.zh: 東川人並兵南攻中軍，仁厚聞之，大開寨門，設炬火照之，自帥士卒爲兩翼伏道左右。

translations.literal: Dongchuan men united troops south attacked the central army; Renhou heard this, greatly opened camp gates, set torch fires to illuminate, personally led soldiers as two wings ambushed on roads left and right.
translations.idiomatic: The Dongchuan forces combined and attacked the center. When Renhou heard this, he threw open his camp gates, lit torches to blaze the field, and personally led men in ambush on both flanks along the roads.

sentences.zh: 賊至，見門開，不敢入，還去。

translations.literal: Rebels arrived, seeing gates open, dared not enter, returned and left.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy reached the camp, saw the gates wide open, dared not enter, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 仁厚發伏擊之，東川兵大奔，追至城下，蹙之壕中，斬獲甚眾而還。

translations.literal: Renhou released ambush to attack them; Dongchuan troops greatly fled; pursued to below the walls, pressed them into the moat, beheaded and captured very many then returned.
translations.idiomatic: Renhou sprang his ambush. The Dongchuan army broke and fled. He pursued to the walls, drove them into the moat, killed and captured a great many, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 仁厚念諸棄寨走者，明旦所當誅殺甚多，乃密召孔目官張韶，諭之曰：『爾速遣歩探子將數十人分道追走者，自以爾意諭之曰：「僕射幸不出寨，皆不知，汝曹速歸，來旦牙參如常，勿憂也。』」

translations.literal: Renhou thought of those who abandoned camps and fled; next dawn those who ought to be executed and killed would be very many; then secretly summoned document officer Zhang Shao, instructed saying: 'You quickly send foot scouts several tens to divide roads pursue the fleers, on your own with your meaning instruct them saying: "The Delegate fortunately did not leave camp—all did not know—you all quickly return; tomorrow morning muster as usual, do not worry.
translations.idiomatic: Renhou reflected that if he punished every man who had abandoned his post, he would have to execute a great many the next day. He secretly summoned Zhang Shao, his chief clerk, and told him, 'Send foot scouts at once, several dozen in all, by different routes after the fugitives. Tell them in your own words, "The Delegate never left camp and knew nothing of what happened. Return at once. Tomorrow's morning assembly will proceed as usual. You need not fear."

sentences.zh: 韶素名長者，眾信之，至四鼓，皆還寨；

translations.literal: Shao from old was known as elder, masses trusted him; by fourth watch, all returned to camps;'
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shao enjoyed a reputation for honesty, and the men believed him. By the fourth watch they had all returned to camp.'

sentences.zh: 惟楊茂言走至張把，乃追及之。

translations.literal: Only Yang Maoyan fled as far as Zhangba, then was overtaken.
translations.idiomatic: Only Yang Maoyan had fled as far as Zhangba before he was caught.

sentences.zh: 仁厚聞諸寨漏鼓如故，喜曰：「悉歸矣！」

translations.literal: Renhou heard all camps night watches as before, rejoiced saying: "All have returned!"
translations.idiomatic: When Renhou heard the night watches striking as usual in every camp, he said with satisfaction, "They have all come back!"

sentences.zh: 詰旦，諸將牙集，以爲仁厚誠不知也，坐良久，仁厚謂茂言曰：「昨夜聞副使身先士卒，走至張把，有諸？」

translations.literal: Next dawn, all generals mustered; they thought Renhou truly did not know; sat a long while; Renhou said to Maoyan: "Last night I heard the deputy commander took the lead, fled to Zhangba—is it so?"
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the generals assembled for the morning roll call, believing Renhou had been unaware of the rout. They sat a long while before Renhou turned to Yang Maoyan and said, "I heard that last night you led the flight as far as Zhangba. Is that true?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「昨夜聞賊攻中軍，左右言僕射已去，遂策馬參隨，既而審其虛，復還寨中。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Last night I heard rebels attacked the center army; attendants said the Delegate had gone, then spurred horse to follow; afterward verified it was false, again returned to camp."
translations.idiomatic: Maoyan answered, "Last night, when I heard the enemy strike the center, my attendants said you had left. I mounted to follow you, but when I learned it was untrue I came back to camp."

sentences.zh: 仁厚曰：「仁厚與副使俱受命天子，將兵討賊，若仁厚先走，副使當叱下馬，行軍法，代總軍事，然後奏聞。

translations.literal: Renhou said: "Renhou and the deputy commander alike received the Son of Heaven's command, lead troops to punish rebels—if Renhou fled first, the deputy commander ought to shout him down from his horse, apply military law, take overall military affairs in his stead, then memorialize the court.
translations.idiomatic: Renhou said, "You and I both bear the Son of Heaven's commission to campaign against rebels. If I had fled first, you should have ordered me down from my horse, enforced military law, taken command, and then reported to the throne.

sentences.zh: 今副使既先走，又爲欺罔，理當如何？」

translations.literal: Now the deputy commander both fled first and also deceived—by principle what ought to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: You fled first and lied about it. What does military law require?"

sentences.zh: 茂言拱手曰：「當死。」

translations.literal: Maoyan bowed with clasped hands saying: "Ought to die."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Maoyan bowed and said, "Death."

sentences.zh: 仁厚曰：「然！」

translations.literal: Renhou said: "So it is!"
translations.idiomatic: Renhou said, "Quite so."

sentences.zh: 命左右扶下，斬之，諸將股慄。

translations.literal: Ordered attendants to support him down, beheaded him; all generals thighs trembled.
translations.idiomatic: He had attendants lead Yang Maoyan away and beheaded him. Every officer shook with fear.

sentences.zh: 仁厚乃召昨夜所俘虜數十人，釋縛縱歸。

translations.literal: Renhou then summoned last night's captives several tens, released bonds and sent them back.
translations.idiomatic: Renhou then summoned several dozen prisoners taken the night before, freed them, and sent them home.

sentences.zh: 君雄等聞之懼，曰：「彼軍法嚴整如是，自今兵不可復出矣！」

translations.literal: Junxiong and others heard this and feared, saying: "Their military law is so strict and ordered—from now troops cannot again come out!"
translations.idiomatic: When Zheng Junxiong heard of this he said in alarm, "Their discipline is this strict—from now on we dare not sally forth again!"

sentences.zh: 庚辰，時溥遣其將李師悅將兵萬人追黃巢。

translations.literal: On day gengchen, Shi Pu sent his general Li Shiyue to lead troops ten thousand to pursue Huang Chao.
translations.idiomatic: On the day gengchen, Shi Pu sent his general Li Shiyue with ten thousand men in pursuit of Huang Chao.

sentences.zh: 癸未，高仁厚陳於鹿頭關城下，鄭君雄等悉眾出戰。

translations.literal: On day guiwei, Gao Renhou arrayed at Lutou Pass below the walls; Zheng Junxiong and others with all masses came out to battle.
translations.idiomatic: On the day guiwei, Gao Renhou drew up his line before Lutou Pass. Zheng Junxiong led his entire force out to fight.

sentences.zh: 仁厚設伏於陳後，陽敗走。

translations.literal: Renhou set ambush behind the formation, feigned defeat and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Renhou placed an ambush behind his battle line and pretended to flee in defeat.

sentences.zh: 君雄等追之，伏發，君雄等大敗。

translations.literal: Junxiong and others pursued; ambush released, Junxiong and others greatly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Junxiong gave chase; the ambush struck, and his army was routed.

sentences.zh: 是夕，遁歸梓州。

translations.literal: That evening, secretly returned to Zi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: That night they fled back to Zi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 陳敬瑄發兵三千以益仁厚軍，進圍梓州。

translations.literal: Chen Jingxuan sent troops three thousand to augment Renhou's army, advanced to besiege Zi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jingxuan sent three thousand reinforcements to Renhou's army, which then advanced to besiege Zi Prefecture.
